```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Function to calculate season of date
getSeason <- function(input.date){
  numeric.date <- 100*month(input.date)+day(input.date)
  ## input Seasons upper limits in the form MMDD in the "break =" option:
  cuts <- base::cut(numeric.date, breaks = c(0,319,0620,0921,1220,1231)) 
  # rename the resulting groups (could've been done within cut(...levels=) if "Winter" wasn't double
  levels(cuts) <- c("Winter","Spring","Summer","Fall","Winter")
  return(cuts)
}

# Set seed for reproducability
set.seed(1234)
```

Our primary data source for our analysis was Influenza testing data
uploaded to [WHO FluNet](https://who.int/tools/flunet) [@who_flunet]. The following
code-block goes through the data ingestion and basic output cleaning. In
some recent data pulls we've had issues with data formatting, so we have
saved the output of data to file (`co_final.tsv`).

We also pulled in data from transmission zones and coded them in
correspondence to the Ledor S. Igboh publication [@Igboh2023] addressing
potential epidemic zones in Africa. The influenza transmission zone (ITZ)
designation per country was obtained from a second WHO FluNet export
[@who_flunet] (pulled 21 Aug 2025).

```{r}
### FluNET data from WHO (pulled 21 Aug 2025; Melissa Rolfes)

  rename(COUNTRY = COUNTRY_AREA_TERRITORY) %>% 
  select(COUNTRY, ITZ) %>% 
  mutate(COUNTRY = case_when(COUNTRY == "Bolivia (Plurinational State of)" ~ "Bolivia",
                             COUNTRY == "Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)" ~ "Venezuela",
                             COUNTRY == "Iran (Islamic Republic of)" ~ "Iran",
                             COUNTRY == "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland" ~ "United Kingdom",

                             COUNTRY == "occupied Palestinian territory, including east Jerusalem" ~ "Palestine",
                             COUNTRY == "Lao People's Democratic Republic" ~ "Lao PDR",
                             COUNTRY == "Democratic People's Republic of Korea" ~ "North Korea",
```

## 2. Country Categorization {#country-categorization}

For our influenza testing data, we can think of the data itself as a
probability density with a result scale for weeks. However, there is one
critical issue. If our peak of activity falls across yearly transitions,
the data cannot be evaluated properly.

For example, we can look at a mock dataset plot of count densities that
cross a yearly boundary.

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}

co <- read_tsv("data/co_final.tsv") %>% 
  left_join(., itz_co %>% select(-ITZ), by = c("COUNTRY"))


gen_inf_dens <- function(df, variable) {
  ndist <- data.frame(WEEK = 1:52)
  ndist$probability <- dnorm(x = ndist$WEEK, mean = mean(unlist(df[[variable]])), sd = sd(unlist(df[[variable]])))
  return(ndist)
}

# create sequence of weeks
x <- seq(-52, 51, by = 1)
# Choose the mean as 0 and standard deviation as 5
y <- dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = 5)
y <- y * 1000

week_example <- tibble(x,y) %>%
  mutate(YEAR = if_else(x < 0, "Year 1", "Year 2")) %>%
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
  mutate(WEEK = seq_along(YEAR)) %>%
  ungroup()

t_example_plot <- ggplot(week_example, aes(WEEK,y)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(YEAR)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), breaks = c(13,26,39,52), limits = c(1,52))

t_example_plot
```

If our peak activity crosses over a transition the end result for
probability density will place the density in the middle of the period:

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
week_example <- week_example %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(y_dist = list(rep(WEEK, round(y)))) %>%
  ungroup()

# create sequence of weeks
x_p <- seq(1, 52, by = 1)
# Choose the mean as 0 and standard deviation as 5
y_p <- dnorm(x_p, mean = mean(unlist(week_example$y_dist)), sd = sd(unlist(week_example$y_dist)))

week_prob <- tibble(WEEK = x_p, prob = y_p)

week_prob_plot <- ggplot(week_prob, aes(WEEK,prob)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), breaks = c(13,26,39,52), limits = c(1,52))

week_prob_plot
```

To correct for this issue we must assess what proper windows for data
assessment should be.

A convenient way to break up the data to evaluate this is by northern
hemisphere calendar quarters.

We then calculate which quarter has the maximum count density for each
country across seasonal years, which start at week 52 of previous
calendar year to week 51 of the defined seasonal year.

Example: seasonal year 2011 would start at calendar year 2010, week 52
(2010-12-27) and end on 2011, week 51 (2011-12-19).

Note this "seasonal year" (which shifts at week 52) is used only to
classify each country's `max_season` here; it is distinct from the
"shifted year" (which shifts at week 30) introduced below, which is the
week axis actually used for the Q4/Q1 (SY) clustering and GAM analysis
later in the document.

The season that has the most occurrences of being identified as the
maximum in yearly blocks is identified as the `max_season`. If two
seasons have the same number of occurrences as maximums, the total sum
of `INF_ALL` across that country's season occurrences is used as a tie
breaker with the maximum `INF_ALL` sum being taken as priority. If the
sum of `INF_ALL` across seasons is the same, that country is filtered
out, as this is a sign of poor quality data. Country season year blocks
with zero counts or missing data for `INF_ALL` are dropped.

Using this process, a single year of a large volume of submitted data
cannot throw off the overall pattern of seasonal density of submissions
for a given country.

Season years 2011-2019 and 2024 were evaluated for the calculation of
maximum seasonal activity for each country. Season years 2020-2023 are
excluded throughout this analysis because the COVID-19 pandemic
(lockdowns, travel restrictions, and disrupted surveillance) suppressed
normal influenza circulation and reporting, making seasonal patterns
from this period unrepresentative of typical influenza activity.

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}

countries_all_season_zero <- co %>%
  filter((season_year <= 2024 & season_year >= 2011) & season_year %notin% 2020:2023) %>% 
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE) %>%
  summarise(inf_all_sum = sum(INF_ALL, na.rm = T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(inf_all_sum == 0) %>%
  mutate(max_season = NA_character_)
  

countries_dup_max_season <- co %>%
  filter((season_year <= 2024 & season_year >= 2011) & season_year %notin% 2020:2023) %>% 
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, season_year, season) %>%
  summarise(inf_all_season_sum = sum(INF_ALL, na.rm = T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, season_year) %>%
  mutate(max_season = case_when(inf_all_season_sum == max(inf_all_season_sum) &
                                  inf_all_season_sum > 0 ~ season,
                                .default = NA_character_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(is.na(max_season) == F) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, max_season) %>%
  mutate(num_season_occurences = length(max_season),
         inf_all_season_sum_total = sum(inf_all_season_sum)) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE) %>%
  # filter to season(s) with max occurrences of season year max
  filter(num_season_occurences == max(num_season_occurences)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, max_season, num_season_occurences, inf_all_season_sum_total) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE) %>%
  # filter to max occurring season with the max count
  filter(inf_all_season_sum_total == max(inf_all_season_sum_total)) %>%
  # filter out countries with more than one max season if counts are tied
  # indicates poor data
  filter(length(max_season) > 1) %>%
  summarise(max_season = paste0(max_season, collapse = ", ")) %>%
  ungroup()

co_season_max <- co %>%
  filter((season_year <= 2024 & season_year >= 2011) & season_year %notin% 2020:2023) %>% 
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, season_year, season) %>%
  summarise(inf_all_season_sum = sum(INF_ALL, na.rm = T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, season_year) %>%
  mutate(max_season = case_when(inf_all_season_sum == max(inf_all_season_sum) &
                                  inf_all_season_sum > 0 ~ season,
                                .default = NA_character_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(is.na(max_season) == F) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, max_season) %>%
  mutate(num_season_occurences = length(max_season),
         inf_all_season_sum_total = sum(inf_all_season_sum)) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE) %>%
  # filter to season(s) with max occurrences of season year max
  filter(num_season_occurences == max(num_season_occurences)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, max_season, num_season_occurences, inf_all_season_sum_total) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE) %>%
  # filter to max occurring season with the max count
  filter(inf_all_season_sum_total == max(inf_all_season_sum_total)) %>%
  # filter out countries with more than one max season if counts are tied
  # indicates poor data
  filter(length(max_season) < 2) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(q_season = case_when(max_season == "Winter" ~ "Q1",
                              max_season == "Spring" ~ "Q2",
                              max_season == "Summer" ~ "Q3",
                              max_season == "Fall" ~ "Q4"),
         sy_cy = case_when(q_season == "Q1" | q_season == "Q4" ~ "SY", 
                           q_season == "Q2" | q_season == "Q3" ~ "CY"))

co_season_results_summary <- bind_rows(
  countries_all_season_zero %>%
  mutate(max_season = NA_character_,
         num_season_occurences = NA_integer_,
         inf_all_season_sum_total = NA_real_,
         q_season = NA_character_,
         sy_cy = "Excluded: zero INF_ALL counts") %>%
  select(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, max_season, num_season_occurences,
         inf_all_season_sum_total, q_season, sy_cy),
  countries_dup_max_season %>%
    mutate(num_season_occurences = NA_integer_,
           inf_all_season_sum_total = NA_real_,
           q_season = NA_character_,
           sy_cy = "Excluded: more than one max season identified"),
  co_season_max
) %>%
  arrange(COUNTRY) %>%
  ungroup()

# Join data to co to create co_cat for data separation
co_cat <- co %>%
  left_join(co_season_results_summary, by = c("COUNTRY","COUNTRY_CODE")) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  mutate(inf_all_relative = (INF_ALL/sum(INF_ALL, na.rm = T)) * (total_points * 10)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(inf_all_dist = if(is.na(inf_all_relative) | is.nan(inf_all_relative)) {
    list(NA)
  } else {
    list(rep(WEEK, round(inf_all_relative)))
  }) %>%
  ungroup()


# Seasonal summary table
season_tbl <- co_season_results_summary %>% 
  select(sy_cy) %>% 
  tbl_summary(statistic = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)")
 
# Compute country overall max season, filter out countries with zero count maxes and
# countries that have more than one season max (indication of poor data)
co_cat2 <- co_cat %>% 
  group_by(COUNTRY, season) %>%
  summarise(inf_all_rel_season = sum(inf_all_relative, na.rm = T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  mutate(season_max = if_else(inf_all_rel_season == max(inf_all_rel_season), TRUE, FALSE),
         count_of_TRUE = sum(season_max == "TRUE")) %>% 
  mutate(flag_zeromax = case_when(season_max == F ~ "Exclude: Insufficient for timing", T ~ "Include"), 
         flag_GTonemax = case_when(max(count_of_TRUE) > 1 ~ "Exclude: more than 1 max, likely poor data", 
                                   T ~ "Include"))


### Number of countries: this should be a dataframe with 1 row per country. 
### include: 
### - max_season -- which season had the max flu detections
### - flag_GTonemax -- which season had more than 1 Max season, which means that there is probably too little data to tell

  mutate(q_season = case_when(season == "Winter" ~ "Q1",
                                season == "Spring" ~ "Q2",
                                season == "Summer" ~ "Q3",
                                season == "Fall" ~ "Q4"), 
         flag_maxseason = case_when(flag_GTonemax == "Include" ~ q_season, T ~ flag_GTonemax), 
         nh_sh = case_when(flag_maxseason == "Exclude: more than 1 max, likely poor data" ~ "Exclude: more than 1 max, likely poor data", 
                           q_season == "Q1" | q_season == "Q4" ~ "NH", 
                           q_season == "Q2" | q_season == "Q3" ~ "SH"))

### Exclude countries with more than 1 peak or 0 peaks
co_season <- co_cat2 %>%
  filter(flag_zeromax == "Include") %>% #filter(season_max == T) %>%
  filter(flag_GTonemax == "Include") %>% #filter(length(season_max) <= 1 & inf_all_rel_season > 0) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(max_season = season)
```

The plots above show clear sampling density and peaks for countries with
maximum densities in each quarter. Within the plots, the black line is
the start of the calendar year (week 1) and the red line is the start of
a "shifted-year" (week 30). We can see from the outputs that Q1 and Q4
max groups have peak densities cross the calendar year margin, whereas
Q2 and Q3 group's densities cross the shifted year margin. For more
thorough verification we can look at individual country results as well.

```{r}
# Find list of countries that have a minimum number of specified years
# and maximize the number of countries included
find_max_year <- function(data, year_field = "YEAR", min_years = 5) {
  data_tbl <- as_tibble(table(data %>% 
                                  filter(points_in_data_year >= 52) %>%
                                  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE, !!sym(year_field)) %>%
                                  summarise() %>%
                                  ungroup())) %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = COUNTRY_CODE, names_from = !!sym(year_field), values_from = n)
  
  data_tbl <- data_tbl %>% rowwise() %>%
    mutate(total = sum(c_across(matches("^\\d")))) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  data_tbl <- data_tbl %>% filter(total >= min_years)
  
  data_tbl_mat <- data_tbl %>% dplyr::select(matches("^\\d"))
  row.names(data_tbl_mat) <- data_tbl$COUNTRY_CODE
  
  years <- apply(data_tbl_mat, 2, sum)
  max_year <- names(which.max(years))
  
  out_list <- list()
  out_list[["max_year"]] <- max_year
  
  out_list[["max_year_countries"]] <- row.names(data_tbl_mat %>% filter(!!sym(max_year) > 0))
  
  return(out_list)
}

  group_by(COUNTRY, shifted_year) %>%
  mutate(points_in_data_year = length(shifted_week)) %>%
  ungroup()

co_sy_pre_max_year <- find_max_year(co_sy_pre_f, min_years = 5, year_field = "shifted_year")

print(length(c(co_cy_pre_max_year$max_year_countries, co_sy_pre_max_year$max_year_countries)))
```

## 3. Generation of Windowed Generalized Additive Model (`mgcv::gam`)

For each continuous run of weeks within a country (a "country period",
see `data_group` below, which restarts whenever a country has a gap of
more than one calendar/shifted year with no qualifying data), we fit a
univariate GAM of the form

$$\log(E[Y_t]) = \beta_0 + f(t)$$

where $Y_t$ is the weekly count (`INF_ALL`) at date $t$ (`SDATE`) and
$f(t)$ is a smooth function of calendar date. In code, every model fit
in this section has the form:

``` r
gam(INF_ALL ~ s(as.numeric(SDATE), k = <knots>, m = <penalty order>),
    family = poisson(link = "log"), method = "REML",
    na.action = na.omit, data = <country_period_data>)
```

**Family**: a Poisson family with log link was used initially, matching
the count nature of the outcome; the identical model is refit below with
a negative binomial family (`mgcv::nb()`) and the two are compared with
AIC/BIC/dispersion diagnostics, since surveillance counts are frequently
overdispersed relative to Poisson.

**Spline basis**: `s()` uses `mgcv`'s default basis, a thin-plate
regression spline (`bs = "tp"`). This was chosen over a basis requiring
manually-placed knots (e.g. `bs = "cr"`) because country periods vary
widely in length (a few months up to 10 years), and the thin-plate basis
lets `mgcv` place its eigenbasis optimally given only the basis
dimension `k`, with no knot-location decisions needed.

**Basis dimension (`k`)**: `k` is set to 2 per calendar year of data in
the period (knots parameter below), capped at 20 (10 years' worth) for
the longest observed periods. Two knots per year gives the smooth enough
flexibility to resolve a single seasonal peak and trough without
allotting so many basis functions that the GAM could fit week-to-week
noise within a season; `method = "REML"` (below) still penalizes away
any excess variation this allows, so `k` is a flexibility ceiling, not
the realized smoothness.

For the GAM, for each country period, the knots parameter was calculated
for the period data set as:

```         
round(data_group_points/cy_periods)*2 
# or
round(data_group_points/sy_periods)*2
```

**Penalty order (`m`)**: `m = 1` penalizes the first derivative (slope)
of $f(t)$, rather than `mgcv`'s basis-specific default
(second-derivative/ curvature) penalty. A first-derivative penalty was
chosen because weeks at the very edge of a period are sometimes
zero-padded rather than observed (see below); penalizing slope keeps the
fitted curve from extrapolating with a new, steep trend right at those
edges, instead flattening smoothly toward a constant level. For country
periods where \>= 20% of weeks are missing (`gam_m_na`), `m` is instead
left at `mgcv`'s basis-specific default (`m = NA`) rather than fixed at
1, since there isn't enough real signal in a sparse period to reliably
estimate a specific first-derivative penalty.

**Smoothing-parameter selection**: `method = "REML"` is used throughout
instead of `mgcv::gam()`'s default generalized cross-validation
(`"GCV.Cp"`). REML is less prone to under-smoothing and gives more
reliable, better-calibrated smoothing-parameter estimates than GCV,
particularly for the shorter country periods common in this dataset
[@wood2011reml].

**Boundary zero-padding**: zero points are added at week 1 or \>= week
52 of a period specifically where real data is missing there (not for
interior gaps), since influenza activity is reliably near its seasonal
minimum at the boundary between consecutive years in most countries.
This anchors the smooth at the period's edges instead of leaving it to
extrapolate unconstrained from the nearest interior observation.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
# calculate blocks of data years for periods (for gam estimation passing)
co_data_years_cy <- co_cy %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE, YEAR) %>%
  summarise() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE) %>%
  mutate(data_group = cumsum(c(1, diff(YEAR) > 1))) %>%
  ungroup()

# join back information into co_cy
co_cy <- co_cy %>%
  left_join(co_data_years_cy, by = c("COUNTRY_CODE","YEAR")) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE, data_group) %>%
  mutate(data_group_key = seq_along(data_group),
         data_group_points = length(data_group),
         # variable used to determine m setting for gam, m is set to NA if > 20% of data is missing for the data group
         gam_m_na = if_else(sum(is.na(INF_ALL))/data_group_points > 0.20, TRUE, FALSE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE, YEAR) %>%
  mutate(data_year_key = seq_along(YEAR)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(INF_ALL = case_when((WEEK >= 52 & is.na(INF_ALL)) |
                               (WEEK == 1 & is.na(INF_ALL)) ~ 0,
                             .default = INF_ALL),
         INF_A = case_when((WEEK >= 52 & is.na(INF_A)) |
                             (WEEK == 1 & is.na(INF_A)) ~ 0,
                           .default = INF_A),
         INF_B = case_when((WEEK >= 52 & is.na(INF_B)) |
                             (WEEK == 1 & is.na(INF_B)) ~ 0,
                           .default = INF_B))

# calculate the knots parameter by how many periods (52 weeks worth of time) of data there are
cy_periods <- round(length(unique(co_cy$SDATE))/52)

# create gam models for 3 testing variables (INF_ALL, INF_A, INF_B)
# use the data_group_points to calculate the knots parameter
inf_model_cy <- co_cy %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, data_group) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(inf_all_mdl = purrr::map(data, ~ gam(INF_ALL ~ s(as.numeric(SDATE),
                                                          k = round(.x$data_group_points[1]/cy_periods)*2, 
                                                          m = ifelse(.x$gam_m_na[1], NA, 1)),
                                              family = poisson(link="log"),
                                              method = "REML",
                                              na.action=na.omit, data = .x)),
         inf_a_mdl = purrr::map(data, ~ gam(INF_A ~  s(as.numeric(SDATE),
                                                       k = round(.x$data_group_points[1]/cy_periods)*2, 
                                                       m = ifelse(.x$gam_m_na[1], NA, 1)),
                                            family = poisson(link="log"),
                                            method = "REML",
                                            na.action=na.omit, data = .x)),
         inf_b_mdl = purrr::map(data, ~ gam(INF_B ~  s(as.numeric(SDATE),
                                                       k = round(.x$data_group_points[1]/cy_periods)*2, 
                                                       m = ifelse(.x$gam_m_na[1], NA, 1)),
                                            family = poisson(link="log"),
                                            method = "REML",
                                            na.action=na.omit, data = .x))) %>%
  mutate(inf_all_pred = purrr::map2(inf_all_mdl, data, ~ predict(.x, .y, type = "response")),
         inf_a_pred = purrr::map2(inf_a_mdl, data, ~ predict(.x, .y, type = "response")),
         inf_b_pred = purrr::map2(inf_b_mdl, data, ~ predict(.x, .y, type = "response")))

inf_model_values_cy <- dplyr::select(inf_model_cy, -data, -inf_all_mdl, -inf_a_mdl, -inf_b_mdl) %>%
  unnest() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, data_group) %>%
  mutate(data_group_key = seq_along(data_group)) %>%
  ungroup()

# join results back onto data
co_cy <- co_cy %>%
  left_join(inf_model_values_cy, c("COUNTRY", "data_group", "data_group_key"))

# plot out results
g_color_scale <- c("Influenza all - GAM" = "black",
                   "Influenza all - Raw" = "black",
                   "Influenza A - GAM" = "blue",
                   "Influenza A - Raw" = "blue",
                   "Influenza B - GAM" = "orange",
                   "Influenza B - Raw" = "orange")

inf_gam_plot_cy <- co_cy %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=WEEK, group=YEAR)) +
  geom_line(size=0.5, alpha=0.8, aes(y = inf_all_pred, color = "Influenza all - GAM")) +
  geom_line(size=0.5, alpha=0.8, aes(y = inf_a_pred, color = "Influenza A - GAM")) +
  geom_line(size=0.5, alpha=0.8, aes(y = inf_b_pred, color = "Influenza B - GAM")) +
  geom_point(size=0.5, alpha=0.8, shape = 3, aes(y = INF_ALL, color = "Influenza all - Raw")) +
  geom_point(size=0.5, alpha=0.8, shape = 3, aes(y = INF_A, color = "Influenza A - Raw")) +
  geom_point(size=0.5, alpha=0.8, shape = 3, aes(y = INF_B, color = "Influenza B - Raw")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g_color_scale, 
                      limits = names(g_color_scale)) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom') +
  facet_grid_paginate(COUNTRY ~ YEAR, nrow=5, ncol=10, page=1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), breaks = c(13,26,39,52), limits = c(0,53)) +
  ylab('Influenza number positive reported vs. GAM') +
  xlab('Week') +
  theme(axis.text=element_text(size=8),
        axis.title=element_text(size=11),
        plot.title=element_text(size=14, hjust=0.5)) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  guides(colour=guide_legend(ncol=3)) +
  labs(color = NULL)

num_pg_cy <- n_pages(inf_gam_plot_cy)

pdf("plots/inf_gam_vs_raw_cy.pdf", paper = "USr", width = 9)
```

To compare model families, we refit the same three response variables
(`INF_ALL`, `INF_A`, `INF_B`) for the CY partition using a negative
binomial family (`mgcv::nb()`) instead of Poisson, keeping the identical
smoothing (`s()`), knot (`k`), and penalty (`m`) settings used for each
country period above. The negative binomial family relaxes the Poisson
assumption that the mean and variance of counts are equal, which can
better accommodate overdispersed surveillance counts.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
# fit negative binomial equivalents of the CY poisson gams above (same knots/m settings per country period)
inf_model_cy <- inf_model_cy %>%
  mutate(inf_all_mdl_nb = purrr::map(data, ~ gam(INF_ALL ~ s(as.numeric(SDATE),
                                                             k = round(.x$data_group_points[1]/cy_periods)*2, 
                                                             m = ifelse(.x$gam_m_na[1], NA, 1)),
                                                 family = nb(link="log"),
                                                 method = "REML",
                                                 na.action=na.omit, data = .x)),
         inf_a_mdl_nb = purrr::map(data, ~ gam(INF_A ~ s(as.numeric(SDATE),
                                                         k = round(.x$data_group_points[1]/cy_periods)*2, 
                                                         m = ifelse(.x$gam_m_na[1], NA, 1)),
                                               family = nb(link="log"),
                                               method = "REML",
                                               na.action=na.omit, data = .x)),
         inf_b_mdl_nb = purrr::map(data, ~ gam(INF_B ~ s(as.numeric(SDATE),
                                                         k = round(.x$data_group_points[1]/cy_periods)*2, 
                                                         m = ifelse(.x$gam_m_na[1], NA, 1)),
                                               family = nb(link="log"),
                                               method = "REML",
                                               na.action=na.omit, data = .x))) %>%
  mutate(inf_all_pred_nb = purrr::map2(inf_all_mdl_nb, data, ~ predict(.x, .y, type = "response")),
         inf_a_pred_nb = purrr::map2(inf_a_mdl_nb, data, ~ predict(.x, .y, type = "response")),
         inf_b_pred_nb = purrr::map2(inf_b_mdl_nb, data, ~ predict(.x, .y, type = "response")))

inf_model_values_cy_nb <- dplyr::select(inf_model_cy, COUNTRY, data_group,
                                        inf_all_pred_nb, inf_a_pred_nb, inf_b_pred_nb) %>%
  unnest() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, data_group) %>%
  mutate(data_group_key = seq_along(data_group)) %>%
  ungroup()

# join negative binomial predictions back onto data
co_cy <- co_cy %>%
  left_join(inf_model_values_cy_nb, c("COUNTRY", "data_group", "data_group_key"))
```

The GAM fits above visually track the raw weekly counts well for most
country-periods; the diagnostics below assess whether a negative
binomial family improves on this further.

To determine which family fits the data better, we compare the Poisson
and negative binomial GAMs fit for each country period and response
variable using AIC (lower is better). A difference of more than 2 AIC
points ($\Delta AIC = AIC_{Poisson} - AIC_{NB}$) is taken as evidence
favoring one family over the other; smaller differences are treated as
equivalent.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# safely extract AIC (returns NA if a model failed to fit or converge)
safe_aic <- function(mdl) {
  tryCatch(AIC(mdl), error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

gam_family_aic <- bind_rows(
  inf_model_cy %>%
    transmute(COUNTRY, data_group, partition = "CY",
              INF_ALL_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl, safe_aic),
              INF_ALL_nb      = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl_nb, safe_aic),
              INF_A_poisson   = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl, safe_aic),
              INF_A_nb        = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl_nb, safe_aic),
              INF_B_poisson   = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl, safe_aic),
              INF_B_nb        = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl_nb, safe_aic)),
  inf_model_sy %>%
    transmute(COUNTRY, data_group, partition = "SY",
              INF_ALL_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl, safe_aic),
              INF_ALL_nb      = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl_nb, safe_aic),
              INF_A_poisson   = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl, safe_aic),
              INF_A_nb        = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl_nb, safe_aic),
              INF_B_poisson   = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl, safe_aic),
              INF_B_nb        = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl_nb, safe_aic))
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = matches("_(poisson|nb)$"),
               names_to = c("variable","family"),
               names_pattern = "(INF_ALL|INF_A|INF_B)_(poisson|nb)",
               values_to = "aic") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = family, values_from = aic) %>%
  mutate(delta_aic = poisson - nb,
         preferred_family = case_when(is.na(delta_aic) ~ NA_character_,
                                      delta_aic > 2 ~ "Negative binomial",
                                      delta_aic < -2 ~ "Poisson",
                                      TRUE ~ "Equivalent"))

write_tsv(gam_family_aic, "data/gam_family_aic_comparison.tsv", na = "")
```

```{r}
gam_family_aic %>%
  filter(!is.na(preferred_family)) %>%
  select(COUNTRY, data_group, partition, variable, preferred_family) %>%
  arrange(partition, variable) %>%
  rename(Partition = partition, Variable = variable,
         "Preferred family (by AIC)" = preferred_family) %>%
  kable(format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

AIC alone only reflects in-sample fit and can slightly favor the
negative binomial simply because it has one extra free parameter (the
dispersion, $\theta$), even when there is little real overdispersion in
the data. To check this, we add three further diagnostics computed from
the same already-fitted models: BIC (which penalizes that extra
parameter more heavily), the fitted negative binomial $\theta$ itself (a
very large $\theta$ means the negative binomial fit has effectively
collapsed to the Poisson limit), and the Poisson Pearson dispersion
statistic (values near 1 support Poisson; values well above 1 support
negative binomial).

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# safely extract BIC (returns NA if a model failed to fit or converge)
safe_bic <- function(mdl) {
  tryCatch(BIC(mdl), error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

# safely extract the fitted negative binomial theta on its natural (non-log) scale
safe_nb_theta <- function(mdl) {
  tryCatch(mdl$family$getTheta(TRUE), error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

# safely compute the poisson pearson dispersion statistic (~1 supports poisson, >>1 supports negative binomial)
safe_dispersion <- function(mdl) {
  tryCatch(sum(residuals(mdl, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(mdl), error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

gam_family_diagnostics <- bind_rows(
  inf_model_cy %>%
    transmute(COUNTRY, data_group, partition = "CY",
              INF_ALL_bic_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl, safe_bic),
              INF_ALL_bic_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl_nb, safe_bic),
              INF_ALL_theta_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl_nb, safe_nb_theta),
              INF_ALL_dispersion_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl, safe_dispersion),
              INF_A_bic_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl, safe_bic),
              INF_A_bic_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl_nb, safe_bic),
              INF_A_theta_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl_nb, safe_nb_theta),
              INF_A_dispersion_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl, safe_dispersion),
              INF_B_bic_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl, safe_bic),
              INF_B_bic_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl_nb, safe_bic),
              INF_B_theta_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl_nb, safe_nb_theta),
              INF_B_dispersion_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl, safe_dispersion)),
  inf_model_sy %>%
    transmute(COUNTRY, data_group, partition = "SY",
              INF_ALL_bic_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl, safe_bic),
              INF_ALL_bic_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl_nb, safe_bic),
              INF_ALL_theta_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl_nb, safe_nb_theta),
              INF_ALL_dispersion_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_all_mdl, safe_dispersion),
              INF_A_bic_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl, safe_bic),
              INF_A_bic_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl_nb, safe_bic),
              INF_A_theta_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl_nb, safe_nb_theta),
              INF_A_dispersion_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_a_mdl, safe_dispersion),
              INF_B_bic_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl, safe_bic),
              INF_B_bic_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl_nb, safe_bic),
              INF_B_theta_nb = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl_nb, safe_nb_theta),
              INF_B_dispersion_poisson = purrr::map_dbl(inf_b_mdl, safe_dispersion))
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(COUNTRY, data_group, partition),
               names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "^(INF_ALL|INF_A|INF_B)_(bic_poisson|bic_nb|theta_nb|dispersion_poisson)$") %>%
  mutate(delta_bic = bic_poisson - bic_nb,
         bic_preferred_family = case_when(is.na(delta_bic) ~ NA_character_,
                                          delta_bic > 2 ~ "Negative binomial",
                                          delta_bic < -2 ~ "Poisson",
                                          TRUE ~ "Equivalent"))

write_tsv(gam_family_diagnostics, "data/gam_family_diagnostics.tsv", na = "")
```

```{r}
gam_family_diagnostics %>%
  filter(!is.na(bic_preferred_family)) %>%
  select(COUNTRY, data_group, partition, variable, bic_preferred_family) %>%
  arrange(partition, variable) %>%
  rename(Partition = partition, Variable = variable,
         "Preferred family (by BIC)" = bic_preferred_family) %>%
  kable(format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

```{r}
gam_family_diagnostics %>%
  filter(!is.na(theta_nb)) %>%
  group_by(partition, variable) %>%
  summarise(median_theta = round(median(theta_nb), 1),
            pct_theta_gt50 = round(mean(theta_nb > 50) * 100, 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(Partition = partition, Variable = variable,
         "Median fitted NB theta" = median_theta,
         "% country-periods with theta > 50" = pct_theta_gt50) %>%
  kable(format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

```{r}
gam_family_diagnostics %>%
  filter(!is.na(dispersion_poisson)) %>%
  group_by(partition, variable) %>%
  summarise(median_dispersion = round(median(dispersion_poisson), 2),
            pct_overdispersed = round(mean(dispersion_poisson > 1.5) * 100, 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(Partition = partition, Variable = variable,
         "Median Pearson dispersion (Poisson)" = median_dispersion,
         "% country-periods with dispersion > 1.5" = pct_overdispersed) %>%
  kable(format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

The analyses above confirm that the negative binomial model is slightly
preferred, even though the model fits are nearly identical to the
Poisson fitted distributions in most cases.

We will therefore use the negative binomial fitted values forwards for
the subsequent analyses.

## 4. Burden calculations

The testing data across countries varies widely in its depth of
coverage. It has been estimated globally that influenza infects between
5–10% of adults and 20–30% of children yearly [@fischer_global_2014].
These rates will vary per country but we can expect infection rates to
be within the previously mentioned ranges.

With the current data, GAM curve estimations will be used to compute
influenza burden for each yearly window (`inf_all_burden`):

$$inf\_all\_burden = {inf\_all\_pred\_nb_{data\ period\ points} \over \sum inf\_all\_pred\_nb_{data\ period\ points}}$$

```{r}
cal_y_sums <- co_cy %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE, YEAR) %>%
  summarise(sum_inf_all = sum(inf_all_pred_nb, na.rm = T), data_points = length(COUNTRY_CODE))

shifted_y_sums <- co_sy %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE, shifted_year) %>%
  summarise(sum_inf_all = sum(inf_all_pred_nb, na.rm = T), data_points = length(COUNTRY_CODE))

# calculate CY
co_cy <- co_cy %>% 
  mutate(label = paste(COUNTRY, max_season, sep = "-")) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, YEAR) %>%
  mutate(points_in_data_year = length(WEEK)) %>%
  mutate(inf_all_burden = inf_all_pred_nb/sum(inf_all_pred_nb, na.rm = T) *
           (if_else(lubridate::leap_year(YEAR), points_in_data_year/53, points_in_data_year/52))) %>%
  ungroup()

# calculate sy
co_sy <- co_sy %>% 
  mutate(label = paste(COUNTRY, max_season, sep = "-")) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, shifted_year) %>%
  mutate(points_in_data_year = length(shifted_week)) %>%
  mutate(inf_all_burden = inf_all_pred_nb/sum(inf_all_pred_nb, na.rm = T) *
           (if_else(lubridate::leap_year(shifted_year+1), points_in_data_year/53, points_in_data_year/52))) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## 5. Clustering

### 5.1 Split of Data By Years Covered

In order to get a sufficient comparison for the generation of time
series clusters, **a minimum of 5 years of data is required** (\>40% of
the total period of data). Additionally, a minimum of at least one
complete country to country window comparison was required (year or
shifted year). This was done by finding the window with the maximum
country representation and then filtering the dataset to countries
within the maximum representation window.

Splitting of both the SY and CY data sets into `pass` and `hold`
partitions based on the data requirement was completed. Countries within
the `hold` partition with insufficient data for clustering, will be
placed into generated draft clusters later.

```{r}
# Find list of countries that have a minimum number of specified years
# and maximize the number of countries included
find_max_year <- function(data, year_field = "YEAR", min_years = 5) {
  data_tbl <- as_tibble(table(data %>% 
                                  filter(points_in_data_year >= 52) %>%
                                  group_by(COUNTRY_CODE, !!sym(year_field)) %>%
                                  summarise() %>%
                                  ungroup())) %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = COUNTRY_CODE, names_from = !!sym(year_field), values_from = n)
  
  data_tbl <- data_tbl %>% rowwise() %>%
    mutate(total = sum(c_across(matches("^\\d")))) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  data_tbl <- data_tbl %>% filter(total >= min_years)
  
  data_tbl_mat <- data_tbl %>% dplyr::select(matches("^\\d"))
  row.names(data_tbl_mat) <- data_tbl$COUNTRY_CODE
  
  years <- apply(data_tbl_mat, 2, sum)
  max_year <- names(which.max(years))
  
  out_list <- list()
  out_list[["max_year"]] <- max_year
  
  out_list[["max_year_countries"]] <- row.names(data_tbl_mat %>% filter(!!sym(max_year) > 0))
  
  return(out_list)
}

# Get CY set with max country inclusion
co_cy_set <- find_max_year(data = co_cy, year_field = "YEAR", min_years = 5)
# max year is 2019 includes:
# "ARG" "AUS" "BGD" "BOL" "BRA" "BTN" "CHL" "COL" "CUB" "FJI" "HND" "KEN"
# "KHM" "LKA" "MDG" "MMR" "MUS" "NCL" "NPL" "NZL" "PAN" "PER" "PHL" "PRY"
#" SLV" "THA" "UGA" "URY" "VNM" "ZAF" "ZMB"

# Split data into pass and hold partitions
co_cy_pass <- co_cy %>% filter(COUNTRY_CODE %in% co_cy_set$max_year_countries)
co_cy_hold <- co_cy %>% filter(COUNTRY_CODE %notin% co_cy_set$max_year_countries)

# Get CY set with max country inclusion
co_sy_set <- find_max_year(data = co_sy, year_field = "shifted_year", min_years = 5)
# max year is 2015 includes:
# "ALB" "ARM" "AUT" "BEL" "BGR" "BHR" "BLR" "CAN" "CHE" "CHN" "CIV" "CMR"
# "COD" "CRI" "CZE" "DEU" "DNK" "DZA" "ECU" "EGY" "ESP" "EST" "ETH" "FIN"
# "FRA" "GBR" "GEO" "GHA" "GRC" "GTM" "HKG" "HRV" "HUN" "IDN" "IND" "IRL"
# "IRN" "ISL" "ISR" "ITA" "JAM" "JOR" "JPN" "KAZ" "KGZ" "KOR" "LAO" "LBN"
# "LTU" "LUX" "LVA" "MAR" "MDA" "MEX" "MLT" "MNG" "MTQ" "MYS" "NIC" "NLD"
# "NOR" "OMN" "PAK" "POL" "PRT" "QAT" "ROU" "RUS" "SEN" "SGP" "SRB" "SVK"
# "SVN" "SWE" "TGO" "TUN" "TUR" "TZA" "UKR" "USA"
```

```{r}
## Data Preparation
# 2 ============================================================================

# Standardize column names based on dataset type
# COUNTRY_CODE (ISO3) is used as the clustering identifier throughout, since
# it's a stable key. COUNTRY is retained separately as a name lookup table.
standardize_columns <- function(raw_df, dataset_type) {
  year_col <- switch(dataset_type, "calendar" = "YEAR", "shifted" = "shifted_year",
                      stop("DATASET_TYPE must be 'calendar' or 'shifted'"))
  week_col <- switch(dataset_type, "calendar" = "WEEK", "shifted" = "shifted_week",
                      stop("DATASET_TYPE must be 'calendar' or 'shifted'"))

  required_cols <- c("COUNTRY", "COUNTRY_CODE", year_col, week_col, "inf_all_burden")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(raw_df))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) stop("Missing expected columns in RAW_DF: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))

  df <- raw_df %>%
    transmute(
      country      = COUNTRY_CODE,       # clustering identifier (ISO3)
      country_name = COUNTRY,            # retained for labeling
      year_col     = .data[[year_col]],
      week_col     = .data[[week_col]],
      value        = inf_all_burden
    )

  country_lookup <- df %>% distinct(country, country_name) %>% deframe()

  list(df = df, country_lookup = country_lookup)
}

# Build one WIDE matrix per year (rows = countries, cols = weeks)
build_year_matrices <- function(df) {
  years <- sort(unique(df$year_col))
  year_mats <- list()

  for (y in years) {
    wide <- df %>%
      filter(year_col == y) %>%
      select(country, week_col, value) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = week_col, values_from = value) %>%
      arrange(country)

    mat <- as.matrix(wide %>% select(-country))
    rownames(mat) <- wide$country

    complete_rows <- complete.cases(mat)
    if (!all(complete_rows)) {
      warning(sprintf("Year %s: dropping %d countries with incomplete weeks (unexpected given data design)",
                       y, sum(!complete_rows)))
      mat <- mat[complete_rows, , drop = FALSE]
    }

    n_weeks <- ncol(mat)
    year_mats[[as.character(y)]] <- list(
      matrix = mat, n_weeks = n_weeks, weight = n_weeks / WEEK_DENOM, countries = rownames(mat)
    )
  }
  year_mats
}
# ============================================================================

## Base Clustering and Validity Metrics (shared helper functions)
# 3 ============================================================================
run_single_clustering <- function(mat, k, algo) {
  d <- dist(mat, method = "euclidean")

  labels <- switch(algo,
    "kmeans"      = kmeans(mat, centers = k, nstart = 10, iter.max = 50)$cluster,
    "hclust_ward" = cutree(hclust(d, method = "ward.D2"), k = k),
    "hkmeans"     = factoextra::hkmeans(mat, k = k)$cluster,
    "pam"         = cluster::pam(d, k = k)$clustering,
    stop("Unknown algorithm: ", algo)
  )
  names(labels) <- rownames(mat)
  labels
}

# Shared resampling logic: fixed-percentage subsample without replacement
draw_resample_indices <- function(n_year, resample_pct) {
  n_draw <- max(2, round(n_year * resample_pct))
  sample(seq_len(n_year), size = n_draw, replace = FALSE)
}

# Internal validity metrics (reused in ensemble diagnostics + k-selection)
compute_wss <- function(mat, labels) {
  sum(sapply(unique(labels), function(cl) {
    members <- mat[labels == cl, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(members) < 2) return(0)
    center <- colMeans(members)
    sum(rowSums(sweep(members, 2, center)^2))
  }))
}

compute_calinski_harabasz <- function(mat, labels) {
  # CH = (between-cluster SS / (k-1)) / (within-cluster SS / (n-k)). Higher is better.
  n <- nrow(mat); k <- length(unique(labels))
  if (k < 2 || k >= n) return(NA)
  
  overall_center <- colMeans(mat)
  wss <- compute_wss(mat, labels)
  bss <- sum(sapply(unique(labels), function(cl) {
    members <- mat[labels == cl, , drop = FALSE]
    nrow(members) * sum((colMeans(members) - overall_center)^2)
  }))
  (bss / (k - 1)) / (wss / (n - k))
}

compute_dunn_index <- function(mat_or_dist, labels, is_dist = FALSE) {
  # Dunn = min inter-cluster distance / max intra-cluster diameter. Higher is better.
  d <- if (is_dist) as.matrix(mat_or_dist) else as.matrix(dist(mat_or_dist))
  clusters <- unique(labels)
  if (length(clusters) < 2) return(NA)
  
  inter_dists <- c()
  for (i in seq_along(clusters)) for (j in seq_along(clusters)) if (i < j) {
    idx_i <- which(labels == clusters[i]); idx_j <- which(labels == clusters[j])
    inter_dists <- c(inter_dists, min(d[idx_i, idx_j, drop = FALSE]))
  }
  intra_diams <- sapply(clusters, function(cl) {
    idx <- which(labels == cl)
    if (length(idx) < 2) return(0)
    max(d[idx, idx, drop = FALSE])
  })
  if (max(intra_diams) == 0) return(NA)
  min(inter_dists) / max(intra_diams)
}

compute_jaccard_similarity <- function(set1, set2) {
  uni <- length(union(set1, set2))
  if (uni == 0) return(NA)
  length(intersect(set1, set2)) / uni
}

# Verifies that a freshly-assigned names() vector is actually a reordering-safe
# match to its source names
.verify_name_alignment <- function(source_names_before_overwrite, expected_names, context = "") {
  if (length(source_names_before_overwrite) != length(expected_names)) {
    stop(sprintf("Name alignment check failed (%s): length mismatch (%d vs %d)",
                  context, length(source_names_before_overwrite), length(expected_names)))
  }
  if (!is.null(source_names_before_overwrite) &&
      !identical(as.character(source_names_before_overwrite), as.character(expected_names))) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Name alignment check failed (%s): the function's own output names do not match the expected country order.\nThis means names(labels) <- ... would have silently MISALIGNED labels to the wrong countries.\nFirst few mismatches -- got: %s | expected: %s",
      context,
      paste(head(source_names_before_overwrite, 5), collapse = ", "),
      paste(head(expected_names, 5), collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}


# Simple Adjusted Rand Index
compute_ari <- function(labels1, labels2) {
  common <- intersect(names(labels1), names(labels2))
  n <- length(common)

  if (n < 2) {
    warning(sprintf("compute_ari: only %d country(ies) in common between the two label sets -- returning NA", n))
    return(NA)
  }

  tab <- table(labels1[common], labels2[common])
  sum_comb <- function(x) sum(choose(x, 2))
  a <- sum_comb(tab); b <- sum_comb(rowSums(tab)); c <- sum_comb(colSums(tab))
  expected <- (b * c) / choose(n, 2)
  max_index <- (b + c) / 2

  if (is.na(expected) || is.na(max_index) || isTRUE(all.equal(max_index, expected))) return(NA)
  (a - expected) / (max_index - expected)
}

## Build Weighted Co-association Consensus Matrices
# 4 ============================================================================
# Each algorithm gets its own independent consensus matrix per k (not pooled
# together), so algorithms can be compared side-by-side and ONE chosen to
# carry forward. Bootstrap = 100% resample WITH replacement per year; a
# country drawn multiple times is collapsed to one entry before counting
# co-occurrence, so duplicate draws don't inflate pair-weights.
#
# Alongside consensus matrices, this records per-run silhouette, WSS,
# Calinski-Harabasz, and Dunn index (averaged across bootstraps) for each
# (algorithm, k) -- raw clustering-quality metrics computed directly on
# cluster assignments vs. data, NOT derived from the consensus matrix itself.
build_consensus_matrices <- function(year_mats, k_range, algos, n_boot, resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT) {
  all_countries <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(year_mats, `[[`, "countries"))))
  n_all <- length(all_countries)
  knames <- paste0("k", k_range)

  blank_mat <- function() matrix(0, n_all, n_all, dimnames = list(all_countries, all_countries))
  numer <- setNames(lapply(algos, function(a) setNames(lapply(k_range, function(k) blank_mat()), knames)), algos)
  denom <- setNames(lapply(algos, function(a) setNames(lapply(k_range, function(k) blank_mat()), knames)), algos)
  quality <- setNames(lapply(algos, function(a) setNames(
    lapply(k_range, function(k) list(silhouette = c(), wss = c(), calinski_harabasz = c(), dunn = c())),
    knames)), algos)

  total_runs <- length(year_mats) * length(algos) * n_boot * length(k_range)
  pb_counter <- 0

  for (yname in names(year_mats)) {
    ymat <- year_mats[[yname]]$matrix
    weight <- year_mats[[yname]]$weight
    year_countries <- rownames(ymat)
    n_year <- length(year_countries)
    if (n_year < 2) next

    for (algo in algos) {
      for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
        boot_idx <- draw_resample_indices(n_year, resample_pct)
        boot_mat <- ymat[boot_idx, , drop = FALSE]
        unique_present <- rownames(boot_mat)  # no duplicates possible -- sampling without replacement
        if (length(unique_present) < 2) next

        unique_mat <- boot_mat

        for (k in k_range) {
          k_eff <- min(k, length(unique_present))
          if (k_eff < 2) next
          kname <- paste0("k", k)

          labels <- run_single_clustering(boot_mat, k_eff, algo)

          # --- quality metrics ---
          sil <- if (length(unique(labels)) >= 2 && length(unique(labels)) < length(unique_present)) {
            tryCatch(mean(cluster::silhouette(as.integer(labels), dist(unique_mat))[, "sil_width"]),
                      error = function(e) NA)
          } else NA
          q <- quality[[algo]][[kname]]
          q$silhouette <- c(q$silhouette, sil)
          q$wss <- c(q$wss, tryCatch(compute_wss(unique_mat, labels), error = function(e) NA))
          q$calinski_harabasz <- c(q$calinski_harabasz, tryCatch(compute_calinski_harabasz(unique_mat, labels), error = function(e) NA))
          q$dunn <- c(q$dunn, tryCatch(compute_dunn_index(unique_mat, labels), error = function(e) NA))
          quality[[algo]][[kname]] <- q

          # --- co-association tally ---
          present <- unique_present
          for (i in seq_len(length(present) - 1)) {
            ci <- present[i]; li <- labels[ci]
            for (j in (i + 1):length(present)) {
              cj <- present[j]; lj <- labels[cj]
              denom[[algo]][[kname]][ci, cj] <- denom[[algo]][[kname]][ci, cj] + weight
              denom[[algo]][[kname]][cj, ci] <- denom[[algo]][[kname]][cj, ci] + weight
              if (li == lj) {
                numer[[algo]][[kname]][ci, cj] <- numer[[algo]][[kname]][ci, cj] + weight
                numer[[algo]][[kname]][cj, ci] <- numer[[algo]][[kname]][cj, ci] + weight
              }
            }
          }
        }
        pb_counter <- pb_counter + length(k_range)
      }
      cat(sprintf("Finished year %s, algorithm %s (%d/%d runs done)\n", yname, algo, pb_counter, total_runs))
    }
  }

  consensus <- setNames(lapply(algos, function(algo) {
    setNames(lapply(knames, function(kn) {
      cm <- numer[[algo]][[kn]] / denom[[algo]][[kn]]
      diag(cm) <- 1
      cm[is.nan(cm)] <- NA
      cm
    }), knames)
  }), algos)

  quality_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(algos, function(algo) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(k_range, function(k) {
      q <- quality[[algo]][[paste0("k", k)]]
      data.frame(algorithm = algo, k = k,
                 mean_silhouette = mean(q$silhouette, na.rm = TRUE), sd_silhouette = sd(q$silhouette, na.rm = TRUE),
                 mean_wss = mean(q$wss, na.rm = TRUE), sd_wss = sd(q$wss, na.rm = TRUE),
                 mean_ch = mean(q$calinski_harabasz, na.rm = TRUE), sd_ch = sd(q$calinski_harabasz, na.rm = TRUE),
                 mean_dunn = mean(q$dunn, na.rm = TRUE), sd_dunn = sd(q$dunn, na.rm = TRUE))
    }))
  }))

  list(consensus = consensus, countries = all_countries, quality_summary = quality_summary)
}

## Ensemble Diagnostics (compare the 4 base algorithms)
# 5 ============================================================================
# These operate on consensus/algorithm lists to help you pick one algorithm.

# Consensus CDF
plot_consensus_cdf_compare <- function(consensus_by_algo) {
  cdf_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(consensus_by_algo), function(algo) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(consensus_by_algo[[algo]]), function(kname) {
      vals <- consensus_by_algo[[algo]][[kname]][upper.tri(consensus_by_algo[[algo]][[kname]])]
      data.frame(algorithm = algo, k = kname, value = vals[!is.na(vals)])
    }))
  }))
  ggplot(cdf_df, aes(x = value, color = k)) +
    stat_ecdf(geom = "step", linewidth = 0.8) + facet_wrap(~algorithm) +
    labs(title = "Consensus CDF by Algorithm and k", x = "Consensus index value", y = "CDF") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Delta-area (Monti et al. heuristic)
compute_delta_area <- function(consensus_list, k_range) {
  areas <- sapply(names(consensus_list), function(kname) {
    vals <- sort(consensus_list[[kname]][upper.tri(consensus_list[[kname]])])
    vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
    if (length(vals) < 2) return(NA)
    y <- seq_along(vals) / length(vals)
    sum(diff(vals) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
  })
  data.frame(k = k_range, area = areas, delta_area = c(NA, diff(areas) / areas[-length(areas)]))
}

compute_delta_area_compare <- function(consensus_by_algo, k_range) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(consensus_by_algo), function(algo) {
    df <- compute_delta_area(consensus_by_algo[[algo]], k_range); df$algorithm <- algo; df
  }))
}

plot_delta_area_compare <- function(delta_df_compare) {
  ggplot(delta_df_compare, aes(x = k, y = delta_area, color = algorithm)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    labs(title = "Delta-Area by Algorithm",
         x = "k", y = "Relative increase in area") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# PAC (Proportion of Ambiguous Clustering)
compute_pac <- function(consensus_list, lower = 0.1, upper = 0.9) {
  sapply(consensus_list, function(cm) {
    vals <- cm[upper.tri(cm)]; vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
    mean(vals > lower & vals < upper)
  })
}

compute_pac_compare <- function(consensus_by_algo, lower = 0.1, upper = 0.9) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(consensus_by_algo), function(algo) {
    pac_vals <- compute_pac(consensus_by_algo[[algo]], lower, upper)
    data.frame(algorithm = algo, k = names(pac_vals), pac = pac_vals, row.names = NULL)
  }))
}

plot_pac_compare <- function(pac_df_compare) {
  ggplot(pac_df_compare, aes(x = k, y = pac, color = algorithm, group = algorithm)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    labs(title = "Proportion of Ambiguous Clustering (PAC) by Algorithm",
         subtitle = "Lower is more stable", x = "k", y = "PAC") +
    theme_minimal()
}
# ============================================================================

## Silhouette / WSS / CH / Dunn comparison plots
# 6 ============================================================================
# quality_summary: data frame from build_consensus_matrices()$quality_summary
.plot_quality_metric <- function(quality_summary, metric_mean, metric_sd = NULL, title, ylab, higher_better = TRUE) {
  p <- ggplot(quality_summary, aes(x = k, y = .data[[metric_mean]], color = algorithm)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2)
  if (!is.null(metric_sd)) {
    p <- p + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = .data[[metric_mean]] - .data[[metric_sd]],
                                ymax = .data[[metric_mean]] + .data[[metric_sd]]), width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5)
  }
  p + labs(title = title, subtitle = paste("Averaged across bootstrap runs;", if (higher_better) "higher is better" else "lower is tighter"),
            x = "k", y = ylab) + theme_minimal()
}

plot_silhouette_compare <- function(qs) .plot_quality_metric(qs, 
                                                             "mean_silhouette",
                                                             "sd_silhouette",
                                                             "Mean Silhouette Width by Algorithm and k",
                                                             "Mean silhouette width")

plot_wss_compare <- function(qs) .plot_quality_metric(qs,
                                                      "mean_wss",
                                                      NULL,
                                                      "Mean WSS by Algorithm and k",
                                                      "Mean WSS",
                                                      higher_better = FALSE)

plot_ch_compare <- function(qs) .plot_quality_metric(qs,
                                                     "mean_ch",
                                                     "sd_ch",
                                                     "Mean Calinski-Harabasz Index by Algorithm and k",
                                                     "Mean CH index")

plot_dunn_compare <- function(qs) .plot_quality_metric(qs,
                                                       "mean_dunn",
                                                       "sd_dunn",
                                                       "Mean Dunn Index by Algorithm and k",
                                                       "Mean Dunn index")

## Composite algorithm ranking (PAC + silhouette + CH + Dunn, normalized)
# 7 ============================================================================
# Heuristic aid, not a definitive answer.
# Needs check against individual plots and heatmaps/maps before 
# committing to an algorithm.
compute_algorithm_ranking <- function(quality_summary, pac_compare) {
  pac_compare$k <- as.integer(gsub("k", "", pac_compare$k))
  merged <- merge(quality_summary, pac_compare, by = c("algorithm", "k"))

  minmax_norm <- function(x) {
    rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (diff(rng) == 0) return(rep(0.5, length(x)))
    (x - rng[1]) / diff(rng)
  }

  merged %>%
    group_by(k) %>%
    mutate(norm_pac = minmax_norm(1 - pac), norm_sil = minmax_norm(mean_silhouette),
           norm_ch = minmax_norm(mean_ch), norm_dunn = minmax_norm(mean_dunn),
           composite_score = rowMeans(cbind(norm_pac, norm_sil, norm_ch, norm_dunn), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>% arrange(k, desc(composite_score))
}

plot_algorithm_ranking <- function(ranked_df) {
  ggplot(ranked_df, aes(x = k, y = composite_score, color = algorithm)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    labs(title = "Composite Algorithm Ranking (PAC + Silhouette + CH + Dunn, normalized)",
         subtitle = "Higher = better overall; normalized within each k across algorithms",
         x = "k", y = "Composite score (0-1)") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# ============================================================================

## Jaccard resampling stability for one (year, algorithm, k)
# 8 ============================================================================
# Standard cluster-stability approach (Hennig 2007 / fpc::clusterboot logic):
# 1. Cluster the FULL (non-bootstrap) data for a given year/algorithm/k --
#    this is the "reference" clustering.
# 2. For each of n_boot bootstrap resamples, re-cluster and find each
#    reference cluster's BEST-MATCHING cluster in the resample (by Jaccard
#    similarity of member country sets).
# 3. Average the best-match Jaccard score per reference cluster across
#    resamples -- this tells you how "real"/replicable each cluster is.
#
# This is an on-demand diagnostic for a SPECIFIC combination of interest.
# It re-runs clustering independently of build_consensus_matrices() rather
# than reusing its output, since retaining per-resample label sets for every
# (year, algorithm, k) by default would be very memory- and compute-heavy.
compute_jaccard_stability <- function(year_mats, 
                                      year_name, 
                                      algo, k, n_boot = 100, 
                                      resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT,
                                      seed = 1234) {
  set.seed(seed)
  ymat <- year_mats[[year_name]]$matrix
  year_countries <- rownames(ymat)
  n_year <- length(year_countries)
  if (k >= n_year) stop(sprintf("k (%d) must be less than countries in year %s (%d)", k, year_name, n_year))

  ref_labels <- run_single_clustering(ymat, k, algo)
  ref_clusters <- setNames(lapply(unique(ref_labels), function(cl) names(ref_labels)[ref_labels == cl]),
                            paste0("ref_cluster_", unique(ref_labels)))
  best_match <- setNames(lapply(names(ref_clusters), function(x) c()), names(ref_clusters))

  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    boot_idx <- draw_resample_indices(n_year, resample_pct)
    boot_mat <- ymat[boot_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    unique_present <- rownames(boot_mat)
    if (length(unique_present) <= k) next

    labels <- tryCatch(run_single_clustering(boot_mat, k, algo), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(labels)) next
    boot_clusters <- lapply(unique(labels), function(cl) names(labels)[labels == cl])

    for (rc in names(ref_clusters)) {
      jaccards <- sapply(boot_clusters, function(bc) compute_jaccard_similarity(ref_clusters[[rc]], bc))
      best_match[[rc]] <- c(best_match[[rc]], max(jaccards, na.rm = TRUE))
    }
  }

  summary_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ref_clusters), function(rc) {
    scores <- best_match[[rc]]
    data.frame(cluster = rc, n_countries = length(ref_clusters[[rc]]),
               mean_jaccard = mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE), sd_jaccard = sd(scores, na.rm = TRUE),
               stability = cut(mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE), breaks = c(-Inf, 0.5, 0.75, Inf),
                                labels = c("unstable", "moderate", "stable")))
  }))
  list(summary = summary_df, ref_clusters = ref_clusters, ref_labels = ref_labels)
}

# ============================================================================

## Per-year Stability (across all algorithms/k, and across all years)
# 9 ============================================================================
# Answers: "how internally consistent is THIS year's bootstrap clustering,"
# independent of how it combines with other years in the pooled consensus
# matrix.

# Stability summary for one year, across a grid of algorithms x k

compute_year_stability_summary <- function(year_mats, year_name, algos = ALGOS,
                                           k_range = K_RANGE,
                                           n_boot = 100, 
                                           resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT,
                                           seed = 1234) {
  n_year <- length(year_mats[[year_name]]$countries)

  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(algos, function(algo) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(k_range, function(k) {
      if (k >= n_year) return(NULL)  # can't cluster k >= n_countries
      jac <- tryCatch(
        compute_jaccard_stability(year_mats, year_name, algo, k,
                                  n_boot = n_boot,
                                  resample_pct = resample_pct, seed = seed),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (is.null(jac)) return(NULL)
      data.frame(year = year_name, algorithm = algo, k = k,
                 mean_jaccard = mean(jac$summary$mean_jaccard, na.rm = TRUE),
                 min_jaccard  = min(jac$summary$mean_jaccard, na.rm = TRUE),
                 n_clusters   = nrow(jac$summary))
    }))
  }))

  cat(sprintf("\nYear %s stability summary (n = %d countries):\n", year_name, n_year))
  cat(sprintf("Overall mean Jaccard across all (algorithm, k) combinations tested: %.3f\n",
              mean(results$mean_jaccard, na.rm = TRUE)))
  print(results)

  results
}

# ============================================================================

## Run across all years, to compare year-level stability
# 10 ============================================================================
## WARNING: expensive -- runs compute_jaccard_stability() (itself n_boot
## resamples) for EVERY (year, algorithm, k) combination. Consider reducing
## n_boot, algos, or k_range for an initial pass across many years.

compare_year_stability <- function(year_mats, 
                                   algos = ALGOS, k_range = K_RANGE, 
                                   n_boot = 100, resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT,
                                   seed = 1234) {
  all_years <- names(year_mats)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(all_years, function(yname) {
    compute_year_stability_summary(year_mats, yname, 
                                   algos = algos, k_range = k_range, 
                                   n_boot = n_boot, resample_pct = resample_pct,
                                   seed = seed)
  }))
}

plot_year_stability <- function(year_stability_df) {
  summary_by_year <- year_stability_df %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(mean_jaccard = mean(mean_jaccard, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  ggplot(summary_by_year, aes(x = year, y = mean_jaccard, group = 1)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgreen") +
    labs(title = "Mean Resampling Stability (Jaccard) by Year",
         subtitle = "Averaged across all tested algorithms and k",
         x = "Year", y = "Mean Jaccard stability") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

# ============================================================================

## Formal k-selection stats (Elbow, Silhouette-max, CH-peak)
# 11 ============================================================================
# Runs on a SINGLE representative year's full (non-bootstrap) data. It is lighter
# weight than the ensemble machinery. Use this as an independent cross-check
# against the ensemble-based diagnostics.

.kmeans_wss <- function(mat, k) {
  if (k == 1) {
    center <- colMeans(mat)
    return(sum(rowSums(sweep(mat, 2, center)^2)))
  }
  kmeans(mat, centers = k, nstart = 10)$tot.withinss
}

compute_elbow_k <- function(mat, k_range) {
  k_full <- sort(union(1, k_range))
  wss_vals <- sapply(k_full, function(k) .kmeans_wss(mat, k))
  
  x <- (k_full - min(k_full)) / (max(k_full) - min(k_full))
  y <- (wss_vals - min(wss_vals)) / (max(wss_vals) - min(wss_vals))
  x1 <- x[1]; y1 <- y[1]; x2 <- x[length(x)]; y2 <- y[length(y)]
  dist_to_line <- abs((y2 - y1) * x - (x2 - x1) * y + x2 * y1 - y2 * x1) / sqrt((y2 - y1)^2 + (x2 - x1)^2)
  
  candidate_idx <- which(k_full >= 2)
  elbow_k <- k_full[candidate_idx][which.max(dist_to_line[candidate_idx])]
  list(k_range = k_full, wss = wss_vals, elbow_k = elbow_k)
}

compute_silhouette_max_k <- function(mat, k_range) {
  sil_vals <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
    km <- kmeans(mat, centers = k, nstart = 10)
    mean(cluster::silhouette(km$cluster, dist(mat))[, "sil_width"])
  })
  list(k_range = k_range, silhouette = sil_vals, best_k = k_range[which.max(sil_vals)])
}

compute_ch_peak_k <- function(mat, k_range) {
  ch_vals <- sapply(k_range, function(k) compute_calinski_harabasz(mat, kmeans(mat, centers = k, nstart = 10)$cluster))
  list(k_range = k_range, ch = ch_vals, best_k = k_range[which.max(ch_vals)])
}
```
