```{r}
## Plots for each k-selection method
# 12 ============================================================================

# Elbow Method plot
plot_elbow <- function(res, title = "Elbow Method (WSS)") {
  ggplot(data.frame(k = res$k_range, wss = res$wss), aes(k, wss)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = res$k_range) +
    labs(title = title, x = "k", y = "Total WSS") + theme_minimal()
}

# Silhouette-Max plot
plot_silhouette_max <- function(res, title = "Silhouette-Max Method") {
  ggplot(data.frame(k = res$k_range, silhouette = res$silhouette), aes(k, silhouette)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = res$best_k, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = res$k_range) +
    labs(title = title, x = "k", y = "Mean silhouette width") + theme_minimal()
}

# Calinski-Harabasz plot
plot_ch_peak <- function(res, title = "Calinski-Harabasz Peak Method") {
  ggplot(data.frame(k = res$k_range, ch = res$ch), aes(k, ch)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = res$best_k, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = res$k_range) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = sprintf("Suggested k = %d", res$best_k), x = "k", y = "Calinski-Harabasz index") + theme_minimal()
}

# Combined panel: runs all 3 methods on one year's matrix
run_k_selection_panel <- function(mat, k_range = 2:8, seed = 1234) {
  cat("Running elbow method...\n");               elbow_res <- compute_elbow_k(mat, k_range)
  cat("WARNING - Automated elbow selection may be inaccurate!\n")
  cat("Running silhouette-max method...\n");       sil_res   <- compute_silhouette_max_k(mat, k_range)
  cat("Running Calinski-Harabasz peak method...\n"); ch_res  <- compute_ch_peak_k(mat, k_range)
  
  list(elbow = elbow_res, silhouette = sil_res, calinski_harabasz = ch_res)
}

# Returns a list of 3 ggplot objects
# you must explicitly print() each one to see it
plot_k_selection_panel <- function(panel_result) {
  list(elbow = plot_elbow(panel_result$elbow), silhouette = plot_silhouette_max(panel_result$silhouette),
       ch = plot_ch_peak(panel_result$calinski_harabasz))
}
# ============================================================================

## Final Clustering: turn one chosen consensus matrix into discrete clusters
# 13 ============================================================================
# Two families of method, both operating on the SAME consensus matrix for a
# manually-chosen algorithm + k, and both returning an IDENTICAL output shape
# (labels, labels_df, method, graph_obj) so they're interchangeable in
# downstream code (compute_item_consensus, plot_cluster_map, plot_consensus_graph):
#
#   extract_final_clusters()       - hierarchical, average linkage, on (1 - consensus)
#   extract_final_clusters_graph() - louvain / leiden / walktrap / spectral,
#                                    on a graph built from the consensus matrix

# Hierarchical (the conventional consensus-clustering)
# This approach was not used for the final results but was tested
extract_final_clusters <- function(cm, k_final, country_lookup = NULL, linkage = "ward.D2") {
  cm_fill <- cm; cm_fill[is.na(cm_fill)] <- 0
  hc <- hclust(as.dist(1 - cm_fill), method = linkage)
  labels_raw <- cutree(hc, k = k_final)
  
  # cutree() already returns a named vector aligned to the dist/hclust input
  # order -- verify that order actually matches rownames(cm) before trusting
  # the overwrite below, rather than assuming it silently.
  .verify_name_alignment(names(labels_raw), rownames(cm), context = "extract_final_clusters/cutree")
  labels <- labels_raw
  names(labels) <- rownames(cm)
  
  cat(sprintf("Final clustering: hierarchical (%s linkage) on (1 - consensus matrix), k = %d\n", linkage, k_final))
  
  result <- list(labels = labels, hclust_obj = hc,
                 method = sprintf("hclust(linkage='%s') on (1 - consensus matrix), k=%d", linkage, k_final))
  if (!is.null(country_lookup)) {
    result$labels_df <- data.frame(country_code = names(labels), country_name = country_lookup[names(labels)],
                                   cluster = unname(labels)) %>% arrange(cluster, country_name)
  }
  result
}

# Graph-based consensus determination of final clusters from consensus emsemble
# louvain/leiden: resolution-tuned to hit k_final exactly (modularity tiebreak).
# walktrap: native k control via cutree-style cut on its dendrogram.
# spectral: kernlab::specc directly on the consensus matrix (native k control);
extract_final_clusters_graph <- function(cm, k_final, country_lookup = NULL,
                                         algorithm = c("louvain", "leiden", "walktrap", "spectral"),
                                         edge_threshold = 0, resolution_range = seq(0.1, 3, by = 0.05), seed = 1234) {
  algorithm <- match.arg(algorithm)
  set.seed(seed)
  
  cm_fill <- cm; cm_fill[is.na(cm_fill)] <- 0; diag(cm_fill) <- 0
  cm_fill[cm_fill < edge_threshold] <- 0
  g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(cm_fill, mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE, diag = FALSE)
  
  isolated <- igraph::degree(g) == 0
  if (any(isolated)) {
    warning(sprintf("%d countries have no edges above threshold (%g) and are excluded: %s",
                    sum(isolated), edge_threshold, paste(igraph::V(g)$name[isolated], collapse = ", ")))
    g <- igraph::delete_vertices(g, which(isolated))
  }
  active <- igraph::V(g)$name
  n_available <- length(active)
  
  if (algorithm %in% c("louvain", "leiden")) {
    run_comm <- function(r) {
      if (algorithm == "louvain") igraph::cluster_louvain(g, weights = igraph::E(g)$weight, resolution = r)
      else igraph::cluster_leiden(g, weights = igraph::E(g)$weight, objective_function = "modularity", resolution = r)
    }
    # modularity computed from (graph, membership) directly -- cluster_leiden()
    # does not cache a modularity value on its result object the way
    # cluster_louvain() does, so this form is needed to work for both.
    search <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(resolution_range, function(r) {
      comm <- tryCatch(run_comm(r), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(comm)) return(NULL)
      mem <- igraph::membership(comm)
      mod <- tryCatch(igraph::modularity(g, mem, weights = igraph::E(g)$weight), error = function(e) NA)
      list(resolution = r, n_comm = length(unique(mem)), modularity = mod, comm = comm)
    }))
    matching <- Filter(function(x) x$n_comm == k_final, search)
    if (length(matching) == 0) {
      stop(sprintf("No resolution produced k = %d communities. Achieved: %s",
                   k_final, paste(sort(unique(sapply(search, `[[`, "n_comm"))), collapse = ", ")))
    }
    best <- matching[[which.max(sapply(matching, `[[`, "modularity"))]]
    mem <- igraph::membership(best$comm)
    
    # membership() is documented to return results in vertex order (matching
    # active/V(g)$name)
    .verify_name_alignment(names(mem), active, context = sprintf("extract_final_clusters_graph/%s", algorithm))
    labels <- setNames(as.integer(mem), active)
    
    cat(sprintf("Final clustering: %s, resolution = %.3f, k = %d\n",
                algorithm, best$resolution, k_final, best$modularity))
    extra <- list(resolution = best$resolution, modularity = best$modularity, community_obj = best$comm)
    method_str <- sprintf("%s on consensus graph, resolution=%.3f, k=%d", algorithm, best$resolution, k_final)
    
  } else if (algorithm == "walktrap") {
    if (k_final >= n_available) stop(sprintf("k_final (%d) must be less than available countries (%d)", k_final, n_available))
    comm <- igraph::cluster_walktrap(g, weights = igraph::E(g)$weight)
    mem <- igraph::cut_at(comm, no = k_final)
    
    # cut_at() returns a plain unnamed integer vector in vertex order -- unlike
    # membership(), it has no names to check against 'active' directly, but we
    # can still confirm its LENGTH matches before blindly assigning names.
    if (length(mem) != length(active)) {
      stop(sprintf("Name alignment check failed (walktrap): cut_at() returned %d labels for %d active vertices",
                   length(mem), length(active)))
    }
    labels <- setNames(as.integer(mem), active)
    mod <- tryCatch(igraph::modularity(g, mem, weights = igraph::E(g)$weight), error = function(e) NA)
    
    cat(sprintf("Final clustering: walktrap, k = %d\n", k_final, mod))
    extra <- list(modularity = mod, community_obj = comm)
    method_str <- sprintf("walktrap on consensus graph, k=%d", k_final)
    
  } else { # spectral
    if (k_final >= n_available) stop(sprintf("k_final (%d) must be less than available countries (%d)", k_final, n_available))
    sim_mat <- cm_fill[active, active]   # explicit reordering to 'active' order
    spec_result <- kernlab::specc(kernlab::as.kernelMatrix(sim_mat), centers = k_final)
    
    # specc() returns a plain unnamed cluster-assignment vector in the same row
    # order as its input kernel matrix (sim_mat, explicitly ordered by
    # 'active'). Verify length as a sanity check before assigning names.
    spec_labels <- as.integer(spec_result@.Data)
    if (length(spec_labels) != length(active)) {
      stop(sprintf("Name alignment check failed (spectral): specc() returned %d labels for %d active countries",
                   length(spec_labels), length(active)))
    }
    labels <- setNames(spec_labels, active)
    mod <- tryCatch(igraph::modularity(g, labels, weights = igraph::E(g)$weight), error = function(e) NA)
    
    cat(sprintf("Final clustering: spectral (kernlab::specc), k = %d\n", k_final, mod))
    cat("(graph_obj built afterward for plotting only -- clustering used the consensus matrix directly)\n")
    extra <- list(modularity = mod, specc_obj = spec_result)
    method_str <- sprintf("spectral (kernlab::specc) on consensus matrix, k=%d", k_final)
  }
  
  if (any(isolated)) cat(sprintf("(%d isolated countries excluded -- see warning above)\n", sum(isolated)))
  
  result <- c(list(labels = labels, graph_obj = g, method = method_str), extra)
  if (!is.null(country_lookup)) {
    result$labels_df <- data.frame(country_code = names(labels), country_name = country_lookup[names(labels)],
                                   cluster = unname(labels)) %>% arrange(cluster, country_name)
  }
  result
}

# Compare final-clustering methods against each other (ARI)
compare_final_clustering_methods <- function(cm, k_final, country_lookup = NULL, graph_algorithm = "louvain") {
  hier  <- extract_final_clusters(cm, k_final, country_lookup = country_lookup)
  graph <- extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k_final, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = graph_algorithm)
  common <- intersect(names(hier$labels), names(graph$labels))
  ari <- compute_ari(hier$labels, graph$labels)
  
  comparison_df <- data.frame(
    country_code = common,
    country_name = if (!is.null(country_lookup)) country_lookup[common] else NA,
    hierarchical_cluster = hier$labels[common], graph_cluster = graph$labels[common]
  ) %>% arrange(hierarchical_cluster, graph_cluster)
  
  cat(sprintf("\nAgreement (hierarchical vs %s): ARI = %.4f (1 = identical, 0 = random)\n", graph_algorithm, ari))
  cat(sprintf("Compared on %d common countries\n", length(common)))
  if (length(common) < length(hier$labels)) {
    cat(sprintf("Note: %d countries excluded from graph method (isolated)\n", length(hier$labels) - length(common)))
  }
  list(hierarchical = hier, graph = graph, ari = ari, comparison_df = comparison_df)
}

# Compare ALL 5 final-clustering methods at once (pairwise ARI matrix)
compare_all_clustering_methods <- function(cm, k_final, country_lookup = NULL) {
  method_fns <- list(
    hierarchical = function() extract_final_clusters(cm, k_final, country_lookup = country_lookup),
    louvain  = function() extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k_final, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "louvain"),
    leiden   = function() extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k_final, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "leiden"),
    walktrap = function() extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k_final, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "walktrap"),
    spectral = function() extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k_final, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "spectral")
  )
  
  # Iterate over method_fns DIRECTLY (not names(method_fns)) so lapply
  # preserves the list names automatically
  results_raw <- lapply(method_fns, function(fn) {
    tryCatch(fn(), error = function(e) { warning(conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  })
  results <- Filter(Negate(is.null), results_raw)
  
  if (length(results) == 0) stop("All clustering methods failed -- check warnings above for details.")
  if (length(results) < length(method_fns)) {
    failed <- setdiff(names(method_fns), names(results))
    cat(sprintf("Note: %d method(s) failed and were excluded: %s\n", length(failed), paste(failed, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  # Diagnostic: how many countries did each method actually produce labels
  # for? Graph-based methods silently exclude isolated (zero-edge) countries,
  # so coverage can legitimately differ between methods
  coverage <- sapply(results, function(r) length(r$labels))
  cat("\nCountries covered by each method:\n"); print(coverage)
  if (length(unique(coverage)) > 1) {
    cat("Note: coverage differs across methods -- likely due to isolated/zero-weight-edge\n")
    cat("countries being excluded by graph-based methods but not by hierarchical clustering.\n")
    cat("Pairwise ARI below is computed only on each pair's COMMON countries.\n")
  }
  
  mn <- names(results)
  ari_matrix <- matrix(NA, length(mn), length(mn), dimnames = list(mn, mn))
  for (i in seq_along(mn)) for (j in seq_along(mn)) {
    ari_matrix[i, j] <- compute_ari(results[[mn[i]]]$labels, results[[mn[j]]]$labels)
  }
  cat("\nPairwise Adjusted Rand Index across methods:\n"); print(round(ari_matrix, 3))
  list(results = results, ari_matrix = ari_matrix, coverage = coverage)
}

## Diagnostics on the Final Clustering Output
# 14 ============================================================================

# Consensus heatmap for a specific algorithm + k
plot_consensus_heatmap <- function(cm, order_countries = NULL, title = "", country_lookup = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(order_countries)) {
    cm <- cm[order_countries, order_countries]
  } else {
    cm_fill <- cm; cm_fill[is.na(cm_fill)] <- 0
    hc <- hclust(as.dist(1 - cm_fill), method = "average")
    cm <- cm[hc$order, hc$order]
  }
  if (!is.null(country_lookup)) { rownames(cm) <- country_lookup[rownames(cm)]; colnames(cm) <- country_lookup[colnames(cm)] }
  
  melted <- melt(cm, varnames = c("Country1", "Country2"), value.name = "Consensus")
  ggplot(melted, aes(Country1, Country2, fill = Consensus)) +
    geom_tile() + scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkred", na.value = "grey90") +
    theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 6), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6)) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = NULL)
}

# Item consensus: per-country stability within its assigned cluster
# Averages this country's pairwise consensus value against every
# other member of its own final cluster. This is a proxy for "how often did
# this country run with its final group," expressed as an averaged pairwise
# agreement score
compute_item_consensus <- function(cm, final_labels) {
  countries <- names(final_labels)
  sapply(countries, function(ci) {
    same <- countries[final_labels == final_labels[ci] & countries != ci]
    if (length(same) == 0) return(NA)
    mean(cm[ci, same], na.rm = TRUE)
  })
}

# Literal cluster-membership percentage
# across all bootstrap resamples (for the algorithm/k), answers what
# percentage of the time was this country grouped with the majority of its
# own final cluster's other members? Requires knowing the final
# cluster assignment first
compute_bootstrap_membership_pct <- function(year_mats, final_labels, algo, 
                                             k, n_boot = 100,
                                             resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT,
                                             seed = 1234) {
  set.seed(seed)
  all_countries <- names(final_labels)

  hits <- setNames(rep(0, length(all_countries)), all_countries)
  opportunities <- setNames(rep(0, length(all_countries)), all_countries)

  for (yname in names(year_mats)) {
    ymat <- year_mats[[yname]]$matrix
    year_countries <- rownames(ymat)
    n_year <- length(year_countries)
    if (n_year < 2) next

    for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
      boot_idx <- draw_resample_indices(n_year, resample_pct)
      boot_mat <- ymat[boot_idx, , drop = FALSE]
      unique_present <- rownames(boot_mat)   # no duplicates possible -- sampling without replacement
      if (length(unique_present) < 2) next

      k_eff <- min(k, length(unique_present))
      if (k_eff < 2) next

      resample_labels <- tryCatch(run_single_clustering(boot_mat, k_eff, algo), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(resample_labels)) next

      for (ci in unique_present) {
        if (!(ci %in% all_countries)) next  # skip countries not in final_labels (e.g. excluded as isolated)

        own_cluster <- final_labels[ci]
        own_clustermates <- setdiff(all_countries[final_labels == own_cluster], ci)
        clustermates_present <- intersect(own_clustermates, unique_present)

        opportunities[ci] <- opportunities[ci] + 1
        if (length(clustermates_present) == 0) next

        ci_resample_cluster <- resample_labels[ci]
        same_resample_cluster_mates <- sum(resample_labels[clustermates_present] == ci_resample_cluster)

        if (same_resample_cluster_mates > length(clustermates_present) / 2) {
          hits[ci] <- hits[ci] + 1
        }
      }
    }
  }

  pct <- ifelse(opportunities > 0, 100 * hits / opportunities, NA)
  data.frame(country_code = all_countries, final_cluster = unname(final_labels[all_countries]),
             bootstrap_membership_pct = round(pct, 1), n_opportunities = opportunities,
             row.names = NULL) %>% arrange(final_cluster, desc(bootstrap_membership_pct))
}

# RAW cluster-assignment tally across ALL years/bootstraps:
# This is the rawest possible stability view: for every country, tally how
# many times it was assigned to each cluster, across every bootstrap run and
# every year combined, with no consensus matrix involved.
#
# Cluster labels are arbitrary per run To make raw tallying meaningful, every run's labels are
# first aligned to a single fixed reference clustering via best-overlap
# matching (each run's cluster is mapped to whichever reference cluster it
# shares the most members with). The reference clustering itself is built
# once, from the single most complete year's full data.
# This fixes what "cluster 1," "cluster 2", etc. for the rest of the
# tally, in the same way a reference clustering anchors Jaccard stability
# elsewhere in this pipeline.
#
# Once aligned, a country's raw tally across (aligned_cluster_1_count,
# aligned_cluster_2_count, ..., aligned_cluster_k_count) directly shows
# whether it is consistently assigned to one cluster (e.g. 95/100 in cluster
# 2) or whether its assignment is genuinely SPLIT across clusters (e.g.
# 55/100 cluster 1, 45/100 cluster 2). The latter being a country that
# "shifts clusters" in the most literal, label-level sense.
#
# reference_year: which year's FULL data to build the alignment anchor from
#                 (defaults to the year with the most countries, i.e. the
#                 "anchor year" with maximum coverage).

compute_raw_cluster_tally <- function(year_mats, algo, k, n_boot = 100, resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT, seed = 1234, reference_year = NULL) {
  set.seed(seed)

  if (is.null(reference_year)) {
    reference_year <- names(which.max(sapply(year_mats, function(y) length(y$countries))))
    cat(sprintf("No reference_year specified -- using '%s' (most countries: %d)\n",
                reference_year, length(year_mats[[reference_year]]$countries)))
  }

  ref_mat <- year_mats[[reference_year]]$matrix
  ref_labels <- run_single_clustering(ref_mat, k, algo)

  align_labels <- function(run_labels, ref_labels) {
    common <- intersect(names(run_labels), names(ref_labels))
    if (length(common) == 0) return(NULL)

    overlap <- table(run_labels[common], ref_labels[common])

    mapping <- c()
    used_ref <- c()
    for (r in rownames(overlap)[order(-apply(overlap, 1, max))]) {
      candidates <- overlap[r, ]
      candidates[names(candidates) %in% used_ref] <- -1
      best_ref <- names(candidates)[which.max(candidates)]
      mapping[r] <- best_ref
      used_ref <- c(used_ref, best_ref)
    }

    aligned <- mapping[as.character(run_labels)]
    names(aligned) <- names(run_labels)
    aligned
  }

  all_countries <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(year_mats, `[[`, "countries"))))
  tally <- matrix(0, nrow = length(all_countries), ncol = k,
                   dimnames = list(all_countries, paste0("aligned_cluster_", seq_len(k))))
  n_runs_present <- setNames(rep(0, length(all_countries)), all_countries)

  for (yname in names(year_mats)) {
    ymat <- year_mats[[yname]]$matrix
    year_countries <- rownames(ymat)
    n_year <- length(year_countries)
    if (n_year <= k) next

    for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
      boot_idx <- draw_resample_indices(n_year, resample_pct)
      boot_mat <- ymat[boot_idx, , drop = FALSE]
      unique_present <- rownames(boot_mat)
      if (length(unique_present) <= k) next

      labels <- tryCatch(run_single_clustering(boot_mat, k, algo), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(labels)) next

      aligned <- align_labels(labels, ref_labels)
      if (is.null(aligned)) next

      for (c in names(aligned)) {
        col_idx <- as.integer(aligned[c])
        tally[c, col_idx] <- tally[c, col_idx] + 1
        n_runs_present[c] <- n_runs_present[c] + 1
      }
    }
  }

  tally_df <- as.data.frame(tally)
  tally_df$country_code <- rownames(tally_df)
  tally_df$n_runs_present <- n_runs_present[rownames(tally_df)]

  tally_df$modal_cluster <- apply(tally[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE], 1, function(x) {
    if (sum(x) == 0) return(NA)
    paste0("aligned_cluster_", which.max(x))
  })
  tally_df$shift_score <- apply(tally[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE], 1, function(x) {
    if (sum(x) == 0) return(NA)
    1 - max(x) / sum(x)
  })

  tally_df <- tally_df %>%
    select(country_code, n_runs_present, modal_cluster, shift_score, everything()) %>%
    arrange(desc(shift_score))

  cat(sprintf("\nReference clustering built from year '%s', algorithm '%s', k = %d, resample_pct = %.2f\n",
              reference_year, algo, k, resample_pct))
  cat("\nMost-shifting countries (highest shift_score = assignment most split across clusters):\n")
  print(head(tally_df[, c("country_code", "n_runs_present", "modal_cluster", "shift_score")], 15))

  tally_df
}

# Raw cluster-assignment tally, kept per year:
# Identical alignment mechanism to compute_raw_cluster_tally() (one fixed
# reference clustering, built once; every run's labels aligned to
# it via greedy best-overlap matching), but keeps YEAR as a visible
# dimension in the tally instead of summing across all years into one
# combined count. 
#
# Returns a long-format data frame: one row per (year, country), with that
# year's own tally across aligned clusters and its own shift_score;
# directly comparable to compute_raw_cluster_tally()'s pooled shift_score,
# since both use the same reference clustering/alignment.
compute_raw_cluster_tally_by_year <- function(year_mats, algo, k, 
                                              n_boot = 100,
                                              resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT, 
                                              seed = 1234,
                                              reference_year = NULL) {
  set.seed(seed)

  if (is.null(reference_year)) {
    reference_year <- names(which.max(sapply(year_mats, function(y) length(y$countries))))
    cat(sprintf("No reference_year specified -- using '%s' (most countries: %d)\n",
                reference_year, length(year_mats[[reference_year]]$countries)))
  }

  ref_mat <- year_mats[[reference_year]]$matrix
  ref_labels <- run_single_clustering(ref_mat, k, algo)

  align_labels <- function(run_labels, ref_labels) {
    common <- intersect(names(run_labels), names(ref_labels))
    if (length(common) == 0) return(NULL)
    overlap <- table(run_labels[common], ref_labels[common])

    mapping <- c()
    used_ref <- c()
    for (r in rownames(overlap)[order(-apply(overlap, 1, max))]) {
      candidates <- overlap[r, ]
      candidates[names(candidates) %in% used_ref] <- -1
      best_ref <- names(candidates)[which.max(candidates)]
      mapping[r] <- best_ref
      used_ref <- c(used_ref, best_ref)
    }

    aligned <- mapping[as.character(run_labels)]
    names(aligned) <- names(run_labels)
    aligned
  }

  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(year_mats), function(yname) {
    ymat <- year_mats[[yname]]$matrix
    year_countries <- rownames(ymat)
    n_year <- length(year_countries)
    if (n_year <= k) return(NULL)

    tally <- matrix(0, nrow = n_year, ncol = k,
                     dimnames = list(year_countries, paste0("aligned_cluster_", seq_len(k))))
    n_runs_present <- setNames(rep(0, n_year), year_countries)

    for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
      boot_idx <- draw_resample_indices(n_year, resample_pct)
      boot_mat <- ymat[boot_idx, , drop = FALSE]
      unique_present <- rownames(boot_mat)
      if (length(unique_present) <= k) next

      labels <- tryCatch(run_single_clustering(boot_mat, k, algo), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(labels)) next

      aligned <- align_labels(labels, ref_labels)
      if (is.null(aligned)) next

      for (c in names(aligned)) {
        col_idx <- as.integer(aligned[c])
        tally[c, col_idx] <- tally[c, col_idx] + 1
        n_runs_present[c] <- n_runs_present[c] + 1
      }
    }

    tally_df <- as.data.frame(tally)
    tally_df$country_code <- rownames(tally_df)
    tally_df$year <- yname
    tally_df$n_runs_present <- n_runs_present[rownames(tally_df)]
    tally_df$modal_cluster <- apply(tally, 1, function(x) if (sum(x) == 0) NA else paste0("aligned_cluster_", which.max(x)))
    tally_df$shift_score <- apply(tally, 1, function(x) if (sum(x) == 0) NA else 1 - max(x) / sum(x))

    tally_df
  }))

  results <- results %>%
    select(year, country_code, n_runs_present, modal_cluster, shift_score, everything()) %>%
    arrange(country_code, year)

  cat(sprintf("\nReference clustering built from year '%s', algorithm '%s', k = %d, resample_pct = %.2f\n",
              reference_year, algo, k, resample_pct))
  results
}

# Side-by-side comparison of both cluster country stability measures
compare_stability_measures <- function(cm, final_labels, year_mats, algo, k, n_boot = 100,
                                        resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT, country_lookup = NULL, seed = 1234) {
  cat("Computing item consensus (Option A -- fast, reuses existing consensus matrix)...\n")
  item_cons <- compute_item_consensus(cm, final_labels)

  cat("Computing bootstrap membership percentage (Option B -- re-runs resampling)...\n")
  boot_pct <- compute_bootstrap_membership_pct(year_mats, final_labels, algo, k, n_boot = n_boot,
                                                resample_pct = resample_pct, seed = seed)

  combined <- boot_pct %>%
    mutate(item_consensus = round(item_cons[country_code], 3)) %>%
    { if (!is.null(country_lookup)) mutate(., country_name = country_lookup[country_code], .after = country_code) else . } %>%
    arrange(final_cluster, desc(bootstrap_membership_pct))

  cat("\nCombined stability table (sorted by cluster, then bootstrap membership %):\n")
  print(combined)
  combined
}


# World map of stability metric
# Useful for visually spotting where the geographically weak/ambiguous 
# countries are.
plot_stability_map <- function(values, title = "Cluster Stability by Country",
                                legend_name = "Stability", low_color = "orange",
                                high_color = "steelblue", fix_france = TRUE) {
  world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

  world$iso3_resolved <- ifelse(
    is.na(world$iso_a3) | world$iso_a3 == "-99",
    world$iso_a3_eh,
    world$iso_a3
  )

  if (fix_france) {
    fra_idx <- which(world$iso3_resolved == "FRA")
    if (length(fra_idx) == 1) {
      fra_row <- world[fra_idx, ]
      fra_parts <- tryCatch(sf::st_cast(fra_row, "POLYGON", warn = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (!is.null(fra_parts) && nrow(fra_parts) > 1) {
        bboxes <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(fra_parts)), function(i) sf::st_bbox(fra_parts[i, ]))
        is_mainland <- sapply(bboxes, function(b) b["xmin"] > -6 && b["xmax"] < 12 && b["ymin"] > 40 && b["ymax"] < 52)
        if (any(is_mainland)) {
          mainland_geom <- sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(fra_parts[is_mainland, ]))
          sf::st_geometry(world)[fra_idx] <- sf::st_geometry(sf::st_sf(geometry = mainland_geom))[[1]]
        }
      }
    }
  }

  value_df <- data.frame(iso3_resolved = names(values), stability_value = unname(values))
  world_joined <- world %>% left_join(value_df, by = "iso3_resolved")

  unmatched <- setdiff(names(values), world$iso3_resolved)
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    warning(sprintf("plot_stability_map: %d country code(s) did not match any map country: %s",
                     length(unmatched), paste(unmatched, collapse = ", ")))
  }

  ggplot(world_joined) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = stability_value), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = low_color, high = high_color, na.value = "grey85", name = legend_name) +
    coord_sf(crs = "+proj=robin") + theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = title)
}

# World map of cluster assignments
plot_cluster_map <- function(final_labels, title = "Country Cluster Assignments",
                              fix_france = TRUE) {
  world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

  world$iso3_resolved <- ifelse(
    is.na(world$iso_a3) | world$iso_a3 == "-99",
    world$iso_a3_eh,
    world$iso_a3
  )

  if (fix_france) {
    fra_idx <- which(world$iso3_resolved == "FRA")
    if (length(fra_idx) == 1) {
      fra_row <- world[fra_idx, ]
      fra_parts <- tryCatch(sf::st_cast(fra_row, "POLYGON", warn = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)

      if (!is.null(fra_parts) && nrow(fra_parts) > 1) {
        # Keep only the polygon(s) overlapping mainland Europe's bounding box
        # (roughly lon -5 to 10, lat 41 to 52 covers metropolitan France + Corsica)
        bboxes <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(fra_parts)), function(i) sf::st_bbox(fra_parts[i, ]))
        is_mainland <- sapply(bboxes, function(b) b["xmin"] > -6 && b["xmax"] < 12 && b["ymin"] > 40 && b["ymax"] < 52)

        if (any(is_mainland)) {
          mainland_geom <- sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(fra_parts[is_mainland, ]))
          sf::st_geometry(world)[fra_idx] <- sf::st_geometry(sf::st_sf(geometry = mainland_geom))[[1]]
        }
        # If no piece matches the mainland bounding box, silently leave
        # France's original (combined) geometry in place rather than risk
        # dropping it entirely -- a slightly-too-large France beats no France.
      }
    }
  }

  cluster_df <- data.frame(iso3_resolved = names(final_labels), cluster = factor(unname(final_labels)))
  world_joined <- world %>% left_join(cluster_df, by = "iso3_resolved")

  world_joined$cluster <- factor(ifelse(is.na(as.character(world_joined$cluster)), "No data", 
                                        as.character(world_joined$cluster)),
                                  levels = c(levels(cluster_df$cluster), "No data"))

  unmatched <- setdiff(names(final_labels), world$iso3_resolved)
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    warning(sprintf("plot_cluster_map: %d country code(s) in final_labels did not match any map country: %s",
                     length(unmatched), paste(unmatched, collapse = ", ")))
  }

  cluster_colors <- scales::hue_pal()(nlevels(cluster_df$cluster))
  names(cluster_colors) <- levels(cluster_df$cluster)
  fill_values <- c(cluster_colors, "No data" = "grey85")

  ggplot(world_joined) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = cluster), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values, name = "Cluster") +
    coord_sf(crs = "+proj=robin") + theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = title)
}

# Plot the consensus graph itself (works for any graph-based method output) ----
plot_consensus_graph <- function(graph_result, country_lookup = NULL, min_edge_weight = 0.1, layout = "fr",
                                 node_size = 4, label_nodes = TRUE, title = "Consensus Graph with Community Assignments") {
  g <- graph_result$graph_obj
  labels <- graph_result$labels
  igraph::V(g)$cluster <- factor(labels[igraph::V(g)$name])
  igraph::V(g)$display_name <- if (!is.null(country_lookup)) country_lookup[igraph::V(g)$name] else igraph::V(g)$name
  
  g_plot <- igraph::delete_edges(g, which(igraph::E(g)$weight < min_edge_weight))
  cluster_colors <- scales::hue_pal()(nlevels(igraph::V(g)$cluster))
  names(cluster_colors) <- levels(igraph::V(g)$cluster)
  
  set.seed(1234)
  p <- ggraph::ggraph(g_plot, layout = layout) +
    ggraph::geom_edge_link(aes(edge_alpha = weight, edge_width = weight), color = "grey50") +
    ggraph::scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 2), guide = "none") +
    ggraph::scale_edge_alpha(range = c(0.1, 0.8), guide = "none") +
    ggraph::geom_node_point(aes(color = cluster), size = node_size) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cluster_colors, name = "Cluster") +
    theme_void() + labs(title = title, subtitle = sprintf("Edges below consensus = %.2f hidden for readability", min_edge_weight))
  
  if (label_nodes) p <- p + ggraph::geom_node_text(aes(label = display_name), repel = TRUE, size = 3)
  p
}

# ============================================================================

## Validity indices computed on the CONSENSUS DISTANCE (not raw data)
# 15 ============================================================================
# Given the consensus matrix already built, how good/stable are clusters extracted 
# from it, and what k does the consensus structure itself support? (independent of which base
# algorithm produced it).

compute_consensus_validity <- function(cm, labels) {
  cm_fill <- cm; cm_fill[is.na(cm_fill)] <- 0
  common <- intersect(rownames(cm_fill), names(labels))
  d_mat <- as.matrix(as.dist(1 - cm_fill))[common, common]
  labels <- labels[common]
  n <- length(labels)

  sil <- tryCatch(mean(cluster::silhouette(as.integer(factor(labels)), as.dist(d_mat))[, "sil_width"]), error = function(e) NA)
  # CH needs centroids, which a pure distance matrix lacks -- approximate via classical MDS first
  ch <- tryCatch(compute_calinski_harabasz(cmdscale(d_mat, k = min(n - 2, 10)), labels), error = function(e) NA)
  dunn <- tryCatch(compute_dunn_index(d_mat, labels, is_dist = TRUE), error = function(e) NA)

  data.frame(k = length(unique(labels)), silhouette = sil, calinski_harabasz = ch, dunn = dunn)
}

sweep_consensus_validity <- function(cm, k_range, method_fn, method_name = "method") {
  do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(k_range, function(k) {
    labels <- tryCatch(method_fn(cm, k), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(labels)) return(NULL)
    df <- compute_consensus_validity(cm, labels); df$method <- method_name; df
  })))
}

compare_k_selection_all_methods <- function(cm, k_range, country_lookup = NULL) {
  method_fns <- list(
    hierarchical = function(cm, k) extract_final_clusters(cm, k, country_lookup = country_lookup)$labels,
    louvain  = function(cm, k) extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "louvain")$labels,
    leiden   = function(cm, k) extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "leiden")$labels,
    walktrap = function(cm, k) extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "walktrap")$labels,
    spectral = function(cm, k) extract_final_clusters_graph(cm, k, country_lookup = country_lookup, algorithm = "spectral")$labels
  )
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(method_fns), function(name) sweep_consensus_validity(cm, k_range, method_fns[[name]], name)))
}

plot_consensus_validity_compare <- function(validity_df, metric = c("silhouette", "calinski_harabasz", "dunn")) {
  metric <- match.arg(metric)
  ggplot(validity_df, aes(x = k, y = .data[[metric]], color = method)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Consensus-Matrix %s by Final-Clustering Method and k",
                          switch(metric, silhouette = "Silhouette", calinski_harabasz = "Calinski-Harabasz", dunn = "Dunn Index")),
         subtitle = "Computed on (1 - consensus matrix) distance, not raw weekly data", x = "k", y = metric) +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Plot: shift score trajectory per country across years (line plot)
plot_raw_cluster_shift_by_year <- function(tally_by_year_df, country_lookup = NULL, highlight_countries = NULL) {
  df <- tally_by_year_df
  if (!is.null(country_lookup)) df$country_label <- country_lookup[df$country_code] else df$country_label <- df$country_code

  if (!is.null(highlight_countries)) {
    df <- df %>% filter(country_code %in% highlight_countries)
  }

  ggplot(df, aes(x = year, y = shift_score, group = country_code, color = country_label)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.6) + geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(title = "Raw Cluster-Assignment Shift Score by Country and Year",
         subtitle = "Higher = assignment more evenly split across clusters that year (less stable)",
         x = "Year", y = "Shift score", color = "Country") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          legend.position = if (is.null(highlight_countries)) "none" else "right")
}


# Heatmap: country x year grid of shift score (often more readable
plot_raw_cluster_shift_heatmap <- function(tally_by_year_df, country_lookup = NULL) {
  df <- tally_by_year_df
  if (!is.null(country_lookup)) df$country_label <- country_lookup[df$country_code] else df$country_label <- df$country_code

  # Order countries by their overall mean shift score, so the most-shifting
  # countries (across all years) appear together at the top of the heatmap.
  order_df <- df %>% group_by(country_code) %>%
    summarise(mean_shift = mean(shift_score, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_shift))
  df$country_label <- factor(df$country_label, levels = rev(unique(df$country_label[match(order_df$country_code, df$country_code)])))

  ggplot(df, aes(x = year, y = country_label, fill = shift_score)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue", na.value = "grey85", name = "Shift score") +
    labs(title = "Raw Cluster-Assignment Shift Score by Country and Year", x = "Year", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))
}

plot_raw_cluster_membership_heatmap <- function(tally_by_year_df, country_lookup = NULL) {
  df <- tally_by_year_df
  if (!is.null(country_lookup)) df$country_label <- country_lookup[df$country_code] else df$country_label <- df$country_code

  # Order countries by their overall mean shift score, so the most-shifting
  # countries (across all years) appear together at the top of the heatmap.
  order_df <- df %>% group_by(country_code) %>%
    summarise(mean_shift = mean(shift_score, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_shift))
  df$country_label <- factor(df$country_label, levels = rev(unique(df$country_label[match(order_df$country_code, df$country_code)])))

  ggplot(df, aes(x = year, y = country_label, fill = modal_cluster)) +
    geom_tile() +
    labs(title = "Raw Aligned Cluster-Assignment by Country and Year", x = "Year", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))
}


# ============================================================================

## Full Pipeline Wrapper
# 16 ============================================================================
# Runs all 4 base algorithms independently through the ensemble (Sections 3-4). 
# This does NOT choose a winner, information needs review (quality_summary/pac/delta_area) via
# plots and metrics produced in the pipeline, then manually proceed to final clustering
# of the consensus information via graph methods.


run_consensus_pipeline <- function(raw_df, dataset_type, k_range = K_RANGE, algos = ALGOS, n_boot = N_BOOT, resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT) {
  cat("Standardizing columns for dataset type:", dataset_type, "\n")
  std <- standardize_columns(raw_df, dataset_type)

  cat("Building year matrices...\n")
  year_mats <- build_year_matrices(std$df)

  cat(sprintf("Running ensemble (algorithm x year x resample x k), resample_pct = %.2f, kept separate per algorithm...\n", resample_pct))
  cat("This may take a while depending on data size and n_boot.\n")
  result <- build_consensus_matrices(year_mats, k_range, algos, n_boot, resample_pct = resample_pct)

  list(
    year_mats       = year_mats,
    consensus       = result$consensus,          # consensus[[algo]][[kname]]
    countries       = result$countries,
    country_lookup  = std$country_lookup,
    delta_area      = compute_delta_area_compare(result$consensus, k_range),
    pac             = compute_pac_compare(result$consensus),
    quality_summary = result$quality_summary
  )
}
# ============================================================================
```

### 5.3 Generation and Evaluation of Cluster Ensemble Sets

We will compute country-to-country time series ensembles on data year
windows (calendar/shifted) for each passed data partition
(`co_cy_pass`/`co_sy_pass`) between each country's full set of
year-level burden curves.

The process starts by splitting the data into separate tables by year,
then for each year repeatedly drawing random resamples (without
replacement) of 90% of that year's countries, computing distribution
Euclidean distances, and clustering them.

We chose Euclidean distance as it is the most appropriate distance
metric, as our goal is to group series most critically by their average
epidemic timings. Since our curves are all aligned and normalized, some
of the potential pitfalls of Euclidean distance do not apply for our
dataset (phase penalty, amplitude denomination, etc). The strictness of
the calculation to timing sensitivity, is a feature for our purposes.

We will be testing algorithms of `hclust`, `kmeans`, `pam` and `hkmeans`
over candidate values of k from k = 2 to k = 8. Across all these
resampling runs, the pipeline tracks how often each pair of countries
ends up in the same cluster versus how often they had the chance to,
dividing one by the other to get a consensus score between 0 and 1 for
every pair, with partial years down-weighted in this tally.

This resampling procedure produces a consensus matrix for each algorithm
and k, summarizing how reliably countries cluster together across all
the resampling. From there, diagnostic metrics help to evaluate the
clustering algorithms.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
# Raw data is expected with these ORIGINAL column names:
# Calendar-year data: COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, YEAR,         WEEK,         inf_all_burden
# Shifted-year data:  COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, shifted_year, shifted_week, inf_all_burden

N_BOOT <- 100 # bootstrap resamples per (year, algorithm) for cross algorithm testing
K_RANGE <- 2:8 # k sweep range
ALGOS <- c("kmeans", "hclust_ward", "hkmeans", "pam") # clustering algorithms
WEEK_DENOM <- 52 # weight denominator for partial years
RESAMPLE_PCT  <- 0.9 # fraction of each year's countries drawn

# Calendar-year Pass QC Partition (co_cy_pass)
pipeline_calendar <- run_consensus_pipeline(co_cy_pass,
                                            k_range = K_RANGE, 
                                            algos = ALGOS, 
                                            n_boot = N_BOOT,
                                            resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT,
                                            dataset_type = "calendar")

# Shifted-year Pass QC Partition (co_sy_pass)
pipeline_shifted <- run_consensus_pipeline(co_sy_pass,
                                           k_range = K_RANGE, 
                                           algos = ALGOS, 
                                           n_boot = N_BOOT,
                                           resample_pct = RESAMPLE_PCT,
                                           dataset_type = "shifted")

```

We'll then plot metrics to evaluate clustering algorithm performance for
each partition.

First for the calendar year partition metrics:

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
plot_pac_compare(pipeline_calendar$pac)
plot_delta_area_compare(pipeline_calendar$delta_area)
plot_silhouette_compare(pipeline_calendar$quality_summary)
plot_wss_compare(pipeline_calendar$quality_summary)
plot_ch_compare(pipeline_calendar$quality_summary)
plot_dunn_compare(pipeline_calendar$quality_summary)

algo_ranking <- compute_algorithm_ranking(pipeline_calendar$quality_summary, pipeline_calendar$pac)
plot_algorithm_ranking(algo_ranking)
```

Then for the shifted year partition metrics:

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
plot_pac_compare(pipeline_shifted$pac)
plot_delta_area_compare(pipeline_shifted$delta_area)
plot_silhouette_compare(pipeline_shifted$quality_summary)
plot_wss_compare(pipeline_shifted$quality_summary)
plot_ch_compare(pipeline_shifted$quality_summary)
plot_dunn_compare(pipeline_shifted$quality_summary)

algo_ranking_shifted <- compute_algorithm_ranking(pipeline_shifted$quality_summary, pipeline_shifted$pac)
plot_algorithm_ranking(algo_ranking_shifted)
```

Overall, both `hkmeans` and `kmeans` perform very similarly, with
`kmeans` appearing to have a very slight advantage overall. So we will
select `hkmeans` as the final algorithm to move forwards.

### 5.4 Determination of Ensemble k-value From Anchor Year

To determine the overall final k-value to use for the ensemble
clustering we will compute metrics based on the anchor year of each
dataset. The anchor year is the year which has the most
country-to-country representation in the dataset, which was computed
while creating the `*_pass` data partitions.

First we'll compute assessment metrics for the calendar year partition:

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
anchor_year_matrix <- pipeline_calendar$year_mats[[co_cy_set$max_year]]$matrix
k_panel <- run_k_selection_panel(anchor_year_matrix, k_range = 2:8)

# plot_elbow() RETURNS a list of 3 ggplot objects -- it does NOT
# display them automatically in a script. Print each explicitly:
panel_plots <- plot_k_selection_panel(k_panel)
print(panel_plots$elbow)
print(panel_plots$silhouette)   
print(panel_plots$ch)           
```

Overall, for the calendar year partition, the metrics point to an
optimum k-value of k = 2.

Now we'll repeat the assessment metrics for the shifted year partition:

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
# anchor year matrix and metric calculation
anchor_year_matrix_shifted <- pipeline_shifted$year_mats[[co_sy_set$max_year]]$matrix
k_panel_shifted <- run_k_selection_panel(anchor_year_matrix_shifted, k_range = 2:8)

# plotting of metrics
panel_plots_shifted <- plot_k_selection_panel(k_panel_shifted)
print(panel_plots_shifted$elbow)        
print(panel_plots_shifted$silhouette)   
print(panel_plots_shifted$ch)
```

Overall, for the shifted year partition, the metrics point to an optimal
k-value of k = 3.

Now, we'll set the chosen algorithm and k-values for each data partition
and run a final robust resampling clustering run to generate the final
ensemble sets.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}

K_FINAL     <- 2
K_FINAL_SHIFTED <- 3
```

We can then assess the relative stability of the resampled results per

### 5.5 Final Consensus Clustering from Clustering Ensemble

There are many methods that can be used for determining the final
clustering from an ensemble consensus matrix. This can be done by
computing hierarchical clustering directly from the matrix, or
transforming the matrix into a graph object and using a graph clustering
algorithm. We'll assess our final ensembles by computing the Dunn index
for each of these methods given our final chosen k values and algorithm.

First for the calendar year partition:

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
consensus_validity <- compare_k_selection_all_methods(pipeline_calendar_final$consensus$kmeans$k2,
                                                      k_range = K_FINAL,
                                                      country_lookup = pipeline_calendar$country_lookup)

plot_consensus_validity_compare(consensus_validity, metric = "dunn")
```

And then for the shifted year partition:

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
consensus_validity_shifted <- compare_k_selection_all_methods(pipeline_shifted_final$consensus$kmeans$k3,
                                                              k_range = K_FINAL_SHIFTED,
                                                              country_lookup = pipeline_shifted_final$country_lookup)

plot_consensus_validity_compare(consensus_validity_shifted, metric = "dunn")
```

For both partitions, the `spectral` method performs best, with the Dunn
index serving as the assessment of clustering quality across algorithms.
This makes sense given the nature of spectral clustering. Spectral
clustering should fit well here because of what the consensus matrix
actually looks like structurally. By the time we reach the final
clustering step, the consensus matrix is a dense and fully-weighted
similarity matrix. Spectral clustering works by taking the entire
similarity structure at once, building a graph Laplacian from it, and
finding the eigenvectors that best capture how the whole network
naturally separates [@ng2001spectral]. In this way it's the global
decision based on overall connectivity patterns, which suits our
smoothly-graded, densely-connected matrix.

Given the verification and logical support, we will apply the `spectral`
method for the final clustering results. And then plot the final results
on a global map to see the geographic distribution.

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
final_calendar_clustering <- extract_final_clusters_graph(pipeline_calendar_final$consensus$kmeans$k2,
                                                          K_FINAL,
                                                          country_lookup = pipeline_calendar_final$country_lookup,
                                                          algorithm = "spectral")

                                                         K_FINAL_SHIFTED,
                                                         country_lookup = pipeline_shifted$country_lookup,
                                                         algorithm = "spectral")

                 title = paste("Calendar-Year Consensus Clusters -", CHOSEN_ALGO, "k =", K_FINAL))

plot_cluster_map(final_shifted_clustering$labels, 
                 title = paste("Shifted-Year Consensus Clusters -", CHOSEN_ALGO, "k =", K_FINAL_SHIFTED))
```

Clusters appear to have good relative latitudinal congruence, which is
expected given previous knowledge on influenza seasonality.

### 5.6 Generation of Cluster Distributions

GAM fits were generated for each cluster using all burden data in each
cluster (`inf_all_burden`). Similarly, country GAM fits were also
generated for all passing country data (using `inf_all_burden`).

Clusters from the shifted year partition were initially tagged with "SY"
and clusters from the calendar year partition were tagged with "CY". To
consolidate labeling, the cluster partitions were combined and labeled
A-E. Cluster mapping is as follows:

A = SY1, B = SY3, C = SY2, D = CY2, E = CY1.

`inf_all_burden` is non-negative and right-skewed, with exact zeros
possible in off-season weeks, so each GAM used a Tweedie family
(compound Poisson-Gamma, log link by default) rather than the default
Gaussian, with REML smoothness selection; 95% confidence intervals were
built on the log (link) scale and back-transformed, so they stay
non-negative, then renormalized by the same constant as the fitted
curve. The per-cluster summary curves are hierarchical GAMs: a shared
cyclic smooth over the fitting week is fit alongside a country-specific
factor-smooth term (`bs = "fs"`) that lets each country's curve deviate
from the cluster-level average, following the "global smoother plus
group-level smoothers" approach described in Pedersen et al.
[@pedersen2019hgam]. The reported fit/CI for each cluster excludes the
country-specific term, so it reflects the shared seasonal pattern, but
the shared smooth's own uncertainty is now estimated jointly with the
country-level deviations. Properly widening the CI to reflect
between-country variability in epidemic timing, rather than treating all
country-weeks within a cluster as independent, identically-distributed
observations.

```{r}
# Compute weekly mean of clusters per year, and week

# Combine data with clustering
co_comb_pass <- bind_rows(co_sy_pass, co_cy_pass) %>%
  mutate(combined_cluster = case_when(kmeans_cluster == "SY1" ~ "A",
                                      kmeans_cluster == "SY2" ~ "C",
                                      kmeans_cluster == "SY3" ~ "B",
                                      kmeans_cluster == "CY2" ~ "D",
                                      kmeans_cluster == "CY1" ~ "E"),
         LABEL = paste0(combined_cluster, "-", COUNTRY))

### Week to shifted_week conversion (built first; needed to relabel the GAM axis below)
shifted_wks <- co_sy %>% select(COUNTRY, YEAR, WEEK, shifted_week) %>% filter(COUNTRY == "Albania" & YEAR == 2017) %>% 
  select(WEEK, shifted_week)

# Cluster GAM estimations
# A/B/C (SY-derived) clusters must be fit on shifted_week, not calendar WEEK, or a
# single epidemic spanning the Dec/Jan boundary gets split across the week axis
# (see Section 2); bs = "cc" enforces a smooth cyclic join at week 52 -> week 1.
# inf_all_burden is non-negative, right-skewed, and can be exactly 0 in the
# off-season, which rules out Gamma (requires y > 0); tw() (Tweedie, log link
# by default) handles the zeros while still letting variance scale with the
# mean. method = "REML" gives more reliable smoothness selection and
# better-calibrated CIs than the gam() default (GCV).
# A country-specific factor-smooth (bs="fs") is added so each country can
# deviate from the shared cluster smooth; this absorbs between-country
# correlation into its own term instead of letting it silently narrow the
# cluster-level CI (Pedersen et al. 2019 "GS" hierarchical GAM structure).
inf_cluster_gam <- co_comb_pass %>%
  filter(WEEK < 53) %>%
  mutate(fit_week = if_else(combined_cluster %in% c("A", "B", "C"), shifted_week, WEEK),
         COUNTRY_CODE = factor(COUNTRY_CODE)) %>%
  group_by(combined_cluster, kmeans_cluster) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(inf_clust_mdl = purrr::map(data, ~ gam(inf_all_burden ~ s(fit_week, bs = "cc", k = 30) +
                                                s(fit_week, COUNTRY_CODE, bs = "fs", k = 8,
                                                  xt = list(bs = "cc"), m = 1),
                                                family = tw(),
                                                method = "REML",
                                                knots = list(fit_week = c(0.5, 52.5)),
                                                na.action=na.omit, data = .x)),
         # predict the shared cluster-level curve only (exclude the country-specific
         # factor-smooth) on the link (log) scale so the back-transformed CI can't go negative
         inf_clust_pred = purrr::map2(inf_clust_mdl, data, ~ predict(
           .x,
           newdata = data.frame(fit_week = 1:52,
                                 COUNTRY_CODE = factor(levels(.y$COUNTRY_CODE)[1], levels = levels(.y$COUNTRY_CODE))),
           type = "link", se.fit = TRUE,
           exclude = "s(fit_week,COUNTRY_CODE)"))) %>%
  mutate(inf_clust_fit = purrr::map(inf_clust_pred, ~ exp(.x$fit)),
         inf_clust_lwr = purrr::map(inf_clust_pred, ~ exp(.x$fit - 1.96 * .x$se.fit)),
         inf_clust_upr = purrr::map(inf_clust_pred, ~ exp(.x$fit + 1.96 * .x$se.fit)),
         inf_clust_se = purrr::map(inf_clust_pred, ~ .x$se.fit))

# Basis-dimension (k) adequacy check: an edf near k' signals either the
# shared cyclic smooth or a country-level factor-smooth is too rigid to
# capture its curve shape; re-check after fitting since adding the
# country-specific term changes both smooths' effective degrees of freedom.
cluster_gam_k_check <- inf_cluster_gam %>%
  mutate(k_check = purrr::map(inf_clust_mdl, ~ as.data.frame(mgcv::k.check(.x)))) %>%
  dplyr::select(combined_cluster, kmeans_cluster, k_check) %>%
  unnest(k_check)

cluster_gam_k_check %>%
  kable(format = "html", digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")

inf_cluster_gam_v <- dplyr::select(inf_cluster_gam, -data, -inf_clust_mdl, -inf_clust_pred) %>%
  unnest() %>%
  mutate(fit_week = seq_along(inf_clust_fit)) %>%
  # normalize fit/lwr/upr by the same constant so the CI still brackets the probability curve
  mutate(inf_clust_fit_new = inf_clust_fit / sum(inf_clust_fit),
         inf_clust_lwr_new = inf_clust_lwr / sum(inf_clust_fit),
         inf_clust_upr_new = inf_clust_upr / sum(inf_clust_fit)) %>%
  # restore a calendar WEEK label for display/export (fit_week IS the calendar week for D/E)
  left_join(shifted_wks, by = c("fit_week" = "shifted_week")) %>%
  mutate(WEEK = if_else(combined_cluster %in% c("A", "B", "C"), WEEK, fit_week))

```

A basis-dimension adequacy check (`mgcv::k.check()`) was reviewed
after refitting, since the added country-specific factor-smooth
introduces its own `k'`/edf alongside the shared cyclic smooth's; both
were checked for under-fitting.

We can use the GAM fitted values to find when the influenza epidemics
"typically" start and end for each cluster. We will use the WHO method,
which approximates the start of an epidemic as the 4th week where the
influenza detections exceed the median yearly detections and the end of
the epidemic as the 4th week where the influenza detections fall below
the median yearly detections. Since we have normalized the data, the
parameter we are "monitoring" is the "influenza burden" (which is what
the GAM fitted value represents) over the year. We find the median of
the influenza burden for the epidemic start and end.

```{r}

### Summary of GAM distributions, by cluster, which will help me determine which weeks the bulk of activity occurs during
gam_summaries <- inf_cluster_gam_v %>% 
  group_by(combined_cluster) %>% 
  summarise(sumof = sum(inf_clust_fit_new), 
            meanof = mean(inf_clust_fit_new), 
            q05 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.05), 
            q25 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.25), 
            q50 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.50), 
            q75 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.75), 
            q95 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.95))

# Convert 1D arrays to straight vectors to avoid downstream errors
inf_cluster_gam_v <- inf_cluster_gam_v %>%
  mutate(inf_clust_fit = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_fit)),
         inf_clust_se = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_se)),
         inf_clust_lwr = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_lwr)),
         inf_clust_upr = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_upr)),
         inf_clust_fit_new = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_fit_new)),
         inf_clust_lwr_new = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_lwr_new)),
         inf_clust_upr_new = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_upr_new)))

### merge summaries with GAM fitted values by week
inf_cluster_gam_distn <- left_join(inf_cluster_gam_v, gam_summaries, by = c("combined_cluster")) %>% 
  mutate(respective_week = fit_week) %>%
  arrange(combined_cluster, respective_week) %>% 
  group_by(combined_cluster) %>%
   mutate(
    above_med = !is.na(inf_clust_fit_new) & inf_clust_fit_new >= q50,
    below_med = !is.na(inf_clust_fit_new) & inf_clust_fit_new < q50,
    # new group id each time the logical changes (TRUE<->FALSE) or starts;
    # grouped by combined_cluster so lag()/cumsum() reset at each cluster boundary
    # rather than relying solely on the compound group_by() key further below
    above_grp = cumsum(coalesce(above_med != lag(above_med), above_med)),
    below_grp = cumsum(coalesce(below_med != lag(below_med), below_med))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(combined_cluster, above_grp) %>%
  mutate(above_streak = if_else(above_med, row_number(), 0L),
         above_streak_max = max(above_streak)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Length of each below-median run (0 for above-median blocks); used below to
  # decide which below-median dips are brief enough to bridge over.
  group_by(combined_cluster, below_grp) %>%
  mutate(below_run_length = if_else(below_med, as.integer(n()), 0L)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Bridge brief (<3-week) below-median dips into the surrounding above-median
  # run -- a short-lived dip shouldn't be treated as ending the season; only a
  # genuinely sustained decline (>= 3 weeks below median) counts as a real break.
  mutate(bridged_above = above_med | (below_med & below_run_length < 3)) %>%
  group_by(combined_cluster) %>%
  mutate(bridged_grp = cumsum(coalesce(bridged_above != lag(bridged_above), bridged_above))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(combined_cluster, bridged_grp) %>%
  mutate(bridged_streak = if_else(bridged_above, row_number(), 0L),
         bridged_streak_max = max(bridged_streak)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # The epidemic season's start is the first week of the single longest run of
  # consecutive weeks above the median, after bridging brief dips (must be
  # >= 3 weeks to count as a detectable season). The season's end is the
  # first week of the immediately-following run of weeks below the median
  # (per the WHO-style definition: "the end of influenza epidemics as the
  # first week in which the burden remained below the median for >= 3
  # weeks"). Because bridging already merges any below-median run 
  # <3 weeks into the surrounding above-median run, the run immediately
  # following the chosen longest run is guaranteed (by construction) to
  # already be >= 3 weeks long -- so no separate length check is needed here.
  # If no run reaches 3 weeks, there is no detectable season (start/end = NA).
  # Ties for longest run are broken by taking the chronologically first run.
  #
  # CYCLIC WRAP for "end": the GAM's cyclic spline makes week 52 and week 1
  # part of one continuous annual curve, but run-detection above is linear
  # (lag()/cumsum() don't know the array loops). If the chosen season reaches
  # the array's very last row, there is no "following" group within this one
  # year's window -- but the decline may genuinely continue into the array's
  # own first group (week 1 picks back up right where week 52 left off), so
  # wrap around to group 0 in that case. Two situations are deliberately left
  # as NA rather than risk an incorrect wrapped answer: (1) the season IS
  # group 0 itself with no later group at all (truly no decline all year),
  # and (2) group 0 is itself an above-median run (the season likely spans
  # the array boundary rather than ending there -- not handled by this fix).
  group_by(combined_cluster) %>%
  mutate(season_max_len = suppressWarnings(max(bridged_streak_max[bridged_above & bridged_streak_max >= 3], na.rm = TRUE)),
         is_candidate_season_grp = bridged_above & bridged_streak_max == season_max_len & is.finite(season_max_len),
         season_run_id  = ifelse(any(is_candidate_season_grp), suppressWarnings(min(bridged_grp[is_candidate_season_grp])), NA_integer_),
         is_season_week = !is.na(season_run_id) & bridged_grp == season_run_id,
         respective_epidemic_start = ifelse(any(is_season_week), suppressWarnings(min(respective_week[is_season_week])), NA_integer_),
         group0_is_above = any(bridged_grp == 0 & bridged_above),
         has_direct_next_grp = !is.na(season_run_id) & any(bridged_grp == (season_run_id + 1)),
         end_search_grp = case_when(
           is.na(season_run_id) ~ NA_integer_,
           has_direct_next_grp ~ season_run_id + 1L,
           season_run_id == 0L ~ NA_integer_,
           !group0_is_above ~ 0L,
           TRUE ~ NA_integer_
         ),
         is_end_week = !is.na(end_search_grp) & bridged_grp == end_search_grp,
         respective_epidemic_end = ifelse(any(is_end_week), suppressWarnings(min(respective_week[is_end_week])), NA_integer_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-season_max_len, -is_candidate_season_grp, -season_run_id, -group0_is_above, -has_direct_next_grp, -end_search_grp, -is_end_week)

# min(x, na.rm = TRUE) on an all-NA vector returns Inf (with a warning), not NA --
# this guards the "no detectable season" case (every row NA) so it stays NA
# instead of silently becoming Inf downstream (e.g., in epidemic_start_month).
safe_min_na <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_integer_ else min(x, na.rm = TRUE)

epidemic_thresholds <- inf_cluster_gam_distn %>% 
  group_by(combined_cluster) %>% 
  summarise(respective_epidemic_start = safe_min_na(respective_epidemic_start), 
            respective_epidemic_end = safe_min_na(respective_epidemic_end),
            # % of the cluster's total annual burden (inf_clust_fit_new sums to 1 across
            # all 52 weeks) falling within the epidemic window; wraps across the
            # week-52/week-1 boundary if the window itself does (e.g. start=48, end=6).
            epidemic_burden_pct = if_else(
              is.na(respective_epidemic_start) | is.na(respective_epidemic_end),
              NA_real_,
              100 * sum(inf_clust_fit_new[if (respective_epidemic_start <= respective_epidemic_end) {
                respective_week >= respective_epidemic_start & respective_week <= respective_epidemic_end
              } else {
                respective_week >= respective_epidemic_start | respective_week <= respective_epidemic_end
              }]))) %>% 
  left_join(shifted_wks, c("respective_epidemic_start" = "shifted_week")) %>% rename(calendar_epidemic_start = WEEK) %>%
  left_join(shifted_wks, c("respective_epidemic_end" = "shifted_week"))  %>% rename(calendar_epidemic_end = WEEK) %>%
  mutate(epidemic_start = case_when(combined_cluster %in% c("A", "B", "C") ~ calendar_epidemic_start, 
                                    combined_cluster %in% c("D", "E") ~ respective_epidemic_start), 
         epidemic_start_month = ceiling(epidemic_start / 4.348),
         epidemic_end   = case_when(combined_cluster %in% c("A", "B", "C") ~ calendar_epidemic_end, 
                                    combined_cluster %in% c("D", "E") ~ respective_epidemic_end), 
         epidemic_end_month = ceiling(epidemic_end / 4.348),
         epidemic_burden_pct = round(epidemic_burden_pct, 1)) %>% 
  select(combined_cluster, epidemic_start, epidemic_start_month, epidemic_end, epidemic_end_month, epidemic_burden_pct)
kable(epidemic_thresholds, format = "html", 
      col.names = c("Epidemic zone", 
                    "Week", 
                    "Month", 
                    "Week", 
                    "Month",
                    "% of annual burden")) %>% 
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Epidemic start" = 2, "Epidemic end" = 2, " " = 1)) %>% 
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                    full_width = FALSE) 

```

```{r }
inf_cluster_gam_v <- inf_cluster_gam_v %>%
  left_join(epidemic_thresholds %>%
              select(combined_cluster, epidemic_start, epidemic_end),
            by = c("combined_cluster")) %>%
  mutate(x_start_end = case_when(WEEK == epidemic_start |
                                   WEEK == epidemic_end ~ WEEK,
                                 .default = NA),
         y_start_end = case_when(WEEK == epidemic_start |
                                   WEEK == epidemic_end ~ inf_clust_fit_new,
                                 .default = NA),
         start_end = case_when(WEEK == epidemic_start ~ "epi. start",
                               WEEK == epidemic_end ~ "epi. end",
                               .default = NA)) %>%
  select(-epidemic_start, -epidemic_end)

# Country GAM estimations (same fit_week / cyclic-spline / Tweedie-REML logic as the cluster GAM above)
inf_co_gam <- co_comb_pass %>%
  filter(WEEK < 53) %>%

         inf_clust_pred = purrr::map(inf_clust_mdl, ~ predict(.x, data.frame(fit_week = 1:52), type = "link", se.fit = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(inf_clust_fit = purrr::map(inf_clust_pred, ~ exp(.x$fit)),
```

```{r}
# Convert 1D arrays to numeric to avoid downstream complication
inf_co_gam_v <- inf_co_gam_v %>%
  mutate(inf_clust_fit = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_fit)),
         inf_clust_se = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_se)),
         inf_clust_lwr = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_lwr)),
         inf_clust_upr = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_upr)),
         inf_clust_fit_new = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_fit_new)),
         inf_clust_lwr_new = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_lwr_new)),
         inf_clust_upr_new = as.numeric(drop(inf_clust_upr_new)))

### Summary of GAM distributions, by country, which will help me determine which weeks the bulk of activity occurs during
co_gam_summaries <- inf_co_gam_v %>% 
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>% 
  summarise(sumof = sum(inf_clust_fit_new), 
            meanof = mean(inf_clust_fit_new), 
            q05 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.05), 
            q25 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.25), 
            q50 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.50), 
            q75 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.75), 
            q95 = quantile(inf_clust_fit_new, 0.95))


### merge summaries with GAM fitted values by week
inf_co_gam_distn <- left_join(inf_co_gam_v, co_gam_summaries, by = c("COUNTRY")) %>% 
  mutate(respective_week = fit_week) %>%
  arrange(COUNTRY, respective_week) %>% 
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
   mutate(
    above_med = !is.na(inf_clust_fit_new) & inf_clust_fit_new >= q50,
    below_med = !is.na(inf_clust_fit_new) & inf_clust_fit_new < q50,
    # new group id each time the logical changes (TRUE<->FALSE) or starts;
    # grouped by COUNTRY so lag()/cumsum() reset at each country boundary
    # rather than relying solely on the compound group_by() key further below
    above_grp = cumsum(coalesce(above_med != lag(above_med), above_med)),
    below_grp = cumsum(coalesce(below_med != lag(below_med), below_med))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, above_grp) %>%
  mutate(above_streak = if_else(above_med, row_number(), 0L),
         above_streak_max = max(above_streak)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Length of each below-median run (0 for above-median blocks); used below to
  # decide which below-median dips are brief enough to bridge over.
  group_by(COUNTRY, below_grp) %>%
  mutate(below_run_length = if_else(below_med, as.integer(n()), 0L)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Bridge brief (<3-week) below-median dips into the surrounding above-median
  # run -- a short-lived dip shouldn't be treated as ending the season; only a
  # genuinely SUSTAINED decline (>= 3 weeks below median) counts as a real break.
  mutate(bridged_above = above_med | (below_med & below_run_length < 3)) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  mutate(bridged_grp = cumsum(coalesce(bridged_above != lag(bridged_above), bridged_above))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY, bridged_grp) %>%
  mutate(bridged_streak = if_else(bridged_above, row_number(), 0L),
         bridged_streak_max = max(bridged_streak)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # The epidemic season's START is the first week of the SINGLE LONGEST run of
  # consecutive weeks above the median, after bridging brief dips (must be
  # >= 3 weeks to count as a detectable season). The season's END is the
  # first week of the immediately-following run of weeks below the median
  # (per the WHO-style definition: "the end of influenza epidemics as the
  # first week in which the burden remained below the median for >= 3
  # weeks"). Because bridging already merges any below-median run shorter
  # than 3 weeks into the surrounding above-median run, the run immediately
  # following the chosen longest run is guaranteed (by construction) to
  # already be >= 3 weeks long -- so no separate length check is needed here.
  # If no run reaches 3 weeks, there is no detectable season (start/end = NA).
  # Ties for longest run are broken by taking the chronologically first run.
  #
   # CYCLIC WRAP for "end": the GAM's cyclic spline makes week 52 and week 1
  # part of one continuous annual curve, but run-detection above is linear
  # (lag()/cumsum() don't know the array loops). If the chosen season reaches
  # the array's very last row, there is no "following" group within this one
  # year's window -- but the decline may genuinely continue into the array's
  # OWN first group (week 1 picks back up right where week 52 left off), so
  # wrap around to group 0 in that case. Two situations are deliberately left
  # as NA rather than risk an incorrect wrapped answer: (1) the season IS
  # group 0 itself with no later group at all (truly no decline all year),
  # and (2) group 0 is itself an above-median run (the season likely spans
  # the array boundary rather than ending there -- not handled by this fix).
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  mutate(season_max_len = suppressWarnings(max(bridged_streak_max[bridged_above & bridged_streak_max >= 3], na.rm = TRUE)),
         is_candidate_season_grp = bridged_above & bridged_streak_max == season_max_len & is.finite(season_max_len),
         season_run_id  = ifelse(any(is_candidate_season_grp), suppressWarnings(min(bridged_grp[is_candidate_season_grp])), NA_integer_),
         is_season_week = !is.na(season_run_id) & bridged_grp == season_run_id,
         respective_epidemic_start = ifelse(any(is_season_week), suppressWarnings(min(respective_week[is_season_week])), NA_integer_),
         group0_is_above = any(bridged_grp == 0 & bridged_above),
         has_direct_next_grp = !is.na(season_run_id) & any(bridged_grp == (season_run_id + 1)),
         end_search_grp = case_when(
           is.na(season_run_id) ~ NA_integer_,
           has_direct_next_grp ~ season_run_id + 1L,
           season_run_id == 0L ~ NA_integer_,
           !group0_is_above ~ 0L,
           TRUE ~ NA_integer_
         ),
         is_end_week = !is.na(end_search_grp) & bridged_grp == end_search_grp,
         respective_epidemic_end = ifelse(any(is_end_week), suppressWarnings(min(respective_week[is_end_week])), NA_integer_)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-season_max_len, -is_candidate_season_grp, -season_run_id, -is_season_week, -group0_is_above, -has_direct_next_grp, -end_search_grp, -is_end_week)
 

### epidemic starts and ends for each country
epidemic_thresholds_co <- inf_co_gam_distn %>% 
  group_by(COUNTRY, combined_cluster) %>% 

  summarise(respective_epidemic_start = safe_min_na(respective_epidemic_start), 
            respective_epidemic_end = safe_min_na(respective_epidemic_end)) %>% 
  left_join(shifted_wks, c("respective_epidemic_start" = "shifted_week")) %>% rename(calendar_epidemic_start = WEEK) %>%
  left_join(shifted_wks, c("respective_epidemic_end" = "shifted_week"))  %>% rename(calendar_epidemic_end = WEEK) %>%
  mutate(epidemic_start = case_when(combined_cluster %in% c("A", "B", "C") ~ calendar_epidemic_start, 
                                    combined_cluster %in% c("D", "E") ~ respective_epidemic_start), 
         epidemic_start_month = ceiling(epidemic_start / 4.348),
         epidemic_end   = case_when(combined_cluster %in% c("A", "B", "C") ~ calendar_epidemic_end, 
                                    combined_cluster %in% c("D", "E") ~ respective_epidemic_end), 
         epidemic_end_month = ceiling(epidemic_end / 4.348)) %>% 
  select(COUNTRY, combined_cluster, epidemic_start, epidemic_start_month, epidemic_end, epidemic_end_month)
```
