## 6. Hypothetical Proxying of Countries With Limited Data

When observing the draft clusters generated, there is a strong
latitudinal trend in the resolution. This becomes more evident after
mapping the cluster mean latitudes (by country latitudes weighted by
city populations).

From this simple concept, we can proxy remaining countries with
insufficient (or no) influenza testing data, into the cluster that has
the closest average latitude to the country's latitudinal population
center. If a country has a calculation for a maximum quarter from
[section 2](#country-categorization) that information will be used to
limit the assignment first to only calendar year or shifted year
associated clusters before proxying. If quarter calculation could not be
determined, we will do unrestricted latitudinal proxying.

The map with latitudinal country proxying to draft clusters gives us a
glimpse at what updated epidemic zones could be. City locations and
populations used to compute population-weighted country centroids were
obtained from the GeoNames geographical database [@geonames].

```{r}
# Proxy by latitude

# Obtain dataset of world cities and their population from the maps package
world.cities <- maps::world.cities

# World cities 1000 dataset
world_1000 <- read_tsv("data/cities1000.txt",
                       col_names = c(
                         "geoname_id",
                         "name",
                         "ascii_name",
                         "alternate_names",
                         "latitude",
                         "longitude",
                         "feature_class",
                         "feature_code",
                         "country_code",
                         "cc2",
                         "admin_1_code",
                         "admin_2_code",
                         "admin_3_code",
                         "admin_4_code",
                         "population",
                         "elevation",
                         "dem",
                         "timezone",
                         "modification_date"
                       ))

# Edit maps data to correspond to current country dataset
world_countries <- countrycode(as.character(na.omit(unique(world_1000$country_code))),
                               origin = 'iso2c', destination = 'iso3c')
world_countries[is.na(world_countries == T)] <- c("XKX")

world_countries_names <- countrycode(world_countries,
                               origin = 'iso3c', destination = 'country.name')
world_countries_names[is.na(world_countries_names == T)] <- "Kosovo"

names(world_countries) <- unique(as.character(na.omit(unique(world_1000$country_code))))
world_countries_df <- tibble(country_name = world_countries_names,
                             country_code = names(world_countries),
                             iso3 = world_countries)

# Create avg lat long weighted on population of country cities
world.country.avg.lat.long <- world_1000 %>%
  filter(is.na(country_code) == F) %>%
  left_join(world_countries_df, by = "country_code") %>%
  left_join(co %>% select(COUNTRY_CODE, COUNTRY) %>% distinct(), by = c("iso3" = "COUNTRY_CODE")) %>% 
  group_by(country_name, country_code, iso3, COUNTRY) %>%
  summarise(mean_lat = weighted.mean(latitude, population, na.rm = T),
            mean_long = weighted.mean(longitude, population, na.rm = T)) %>%
  mutate(merged_country = coalesce(COUNTRY,country_name))

### What countries are missing from the world_map but are in our list of cities with lat and long? 
missing.country.name <- world.country.avg.lat.long$merged_country[world.country.avg.lat.long$merged_country %notin%
                                                                  unique(world_map$region)]

### What countries are missing from the list of cities with lat and long but NOT in the world_map? 
missing.region <-  unique(world_map$region)[unique(world_map$region) %notin% 
                                              world.country.avg.lat.long$merged_country]

# Re-code countries
merged_country.dict <- c("Congo" = "Republic of Congo",
                         "Congo Democratic Republic" = "Congo (DRC)",
                         "Czech Republic" = "Czechia",
                         "East Timor" = "Timor-Leste",
                         "Ivory Coast" = "Côte d'Ivoire",
                         "Korea North" = "North Korea",
                         "Korea South" = "Republic of Korea",
                         "Laos" = "Lao PDR",
                         "Madeira" = "Madeira Islands",
                         "Moldova" = "Republic of Moldova",
                         "Pitcairn" = "Pitcairn Islands",
                         "Russia" = "Russian Federation",
                         "Saint Vincent and The Grenadines" = "Saint Vincent and the Grenadines",
                         "Saint-Barthelemy" = "Saint Barthélemy",
                         "Saint-Martin" = "Saint Martin",
                         "Turks and Caicos" = "Turks and Caicos Islands",
                         "UK" = "United Kingdom",
                         "USA" = "United States of America",
                         "Vatican City" = "Vatican",
                         "Vietnam" = "Viet Nam",
                         "Curaçao" = "Curacao",
                         "Réunion" = "Reunion",
                         "Micronesia (Federated States of)" = "Micronesia",
                         "Cocos (Keeling) Islands" = "Cocos Islands",
                         "Syrian Arab Republic" = "Syria",
                         "U.S. Virgin Islands" = "US Virgin Islands",
                         "Wallis & Futuna" = "Wallis and Futuna", 
                         "Tuvalu" = "Tuvalu", 
                         "Tokelau" = "Tokelau")

world.country.avg.lat.long <- world.country.avg.lat.long %>%
  mutate(COUNTRY = if_else(merged_country %notin% unique(world_map$region),
                           as.character(merged_country.dict[merged_country]),
                           merged_country)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(merged_country, iso3, mean_lat, mean_long, COUNTRY)

# Filter out non-map sub regions
world.country.avg.lat.long <- world.country.avg.lat.long %>%
  filter(is.na(COUNTRY) == F)

world_map_addition <- world_map %>%
  filter(region %notin% world.country.avg.lat.long$COUNTRY) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(mean_lat = mean(lat),
            mean_long = mean(long)) %>%
  mutate(merged_country = region,
         iso3 = countrycode(region, origin = 'country.name', destination = 'iso3c'),
         COUNTRY = region) %>%
  select(merged_country, iso3, mean_lat, mean_long, COUNTRY)


# Complete lat long data set
world.country.avg.lat.long <- bind_rows(world.country.avg.lat.long, world_map_addition) %>% 
  mutate(iso3 = case_when(merged_country == "Chagos Archipelago" ~ "IOT", T ~ iso3), 
         )

# Compute cluster average lat long values
cluster.avg.lat.long <- co_comb_pass %>%
  select(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, kmeans_cluster, combined_cluster) %>%
  mutate(cluster_type = "original") %>%
  distinct() %>%
  left_join(world.country.avg.lat.long, by = c("COUNTRY_CODE" = "iso3")) %>%
  group_by(combined_cluster) %>%
  summarise(cl_mean_lat = mean(mean_lat),
            cl_mean_long = mean(mean_long))

# Lat values by clusters
dat.temp <- co_comb_pass %>%
  select(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, kmeans_cluster, combined_cluster) %>%
  mutate(cluster_type = "original") %>%
  distinct() %>%
  left_join(world.country.avg.lat.long, by = c("COUNTRY_CODE" = "iso3")) 

# One-way ANOVA comparing the mean Latitude between zones
anova_lat_result <- aov(mean_lat ~ combined_cluster, data = dat.temp)
# Tidy the ANOVA results and extract the p-value
anova_lat_p_value <- tidy(anova_lat_result) %>%
  filter(term == "combined_cluster") %>%
  select(p.value) %>% 
  mutate(p.value = case_when(p.value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001", 
                           T ~ sprintf("%0.3f", p.value))) %>% 
  pull()

# Dotplot of mean_lat grouped by cluster
mean_lat_plot <- dat.temp %>% 
ggplot(aes(x = combined_cluster, y = mean_lat, group = combined_cluster)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = combined_cluster), 
              size = 3, alpha = 0.8, position = position_jitterdodge()) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = "mean_sdl", fun.args = list(mult = 1), #
    position = position_dodge(width = .75)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("A" = "#DF5C24",
                                "B" = "#7B3A96",
                                "C" = "#059748",
                                "D" = "#E5126F",
                                "E" = "#265DAB"),
                     breaks = c("A","B","C","D","E")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-90, 90), breaks = c(-90, -60, -30, 0, 30, 60, 90)) +
  labs(y = "Population-weighted mean latitude", 
       x = "Epidemic zone") +
  annotate("text", x = "B", y = -85, 
           label = paste0("One-way ANOVA p-value: ", anova_lat_p_value), vjust = -1) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


# Proxy countries by cluster latitude
lat_proxy_cy <- world.country.avg.lat.long %>%
  filter(COUNTRY %notin% c(unique(co_cy_pass$COUNTRY), unique(co_sy_pass$COUNTRY)) &
           COUNTRY %in% (co_season_max %>%
                           filter(q_season %in% c("Q2","Q3")) %>%
                           distinct(COUNTRY) %>% .$COUNTRY)) %>%
  cross_join(cluster.avg.lat.long %>% filter(combined_cluster %in% c("D","E"))) %>%
  mutate(mean_diff = abs(mean_lat - cl_mean_lat)) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  filter(mean_diff == min(mean_diff))

lat_proxy_sy <- world.country.avg.lat.long %>%
  filter(COUNTRY %notin% c(unique(co_cy_pass$COUNTRY), unique(co_sy_pass$COUNTRY)) &
           COUNTRY %in% (co_season_max %>%
                           filter(q_season %in% c("Q1","Q4")) %>%
                           distinct(COUNTRY) %>% .$COUNTRY)) %>%
  cross_join(cluster.avg.lat.long %>% filter(combined_cluster %in% c("A","B","C"))) %>%
  mutate(mean_diff = abs(mean_lat - cl_mean_lat)) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  filter(mean_diff == min(mean_diff))

lat_proxy_ny <- world.country.avg.lat.long %>%
  filter(COUNTRY %notin% c(unique(co_cy_pass$COUNTRY),
                           unique(co_sy_pass$COUNTRY),
                           lat_proxy_cy$COUNTRY,
                           lat_proxy_sy$COUNTRY)) %>%
  cross_join(cluster.avg.lat.long) %>%
  mutate(mean_diff = abs(mean_lat - cl_mean_lat)) %>%
  group_by(COUNTRY) %>%
  filter(mean_diff == min(mean_diff))

# Combine the CY, SY and no partition proxying
lat_proxy <- bind_rows(lat_proxy_cy, lat_proxy_sy, lat_proxy_ny)
  
# Original cluster map data
original_cluster_map <- co_comb_pass %>%
  select(COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, combined_cluster) %>%
  mutate(cluster_type = "original") %>%
  distinct() %>%
  left_join(world.country.avg.lat.long %>% select(COUNTRY, mean_lat, mean_long), by = "COUNTRY")

  left_join(original_cluster_map, by = c("ISO_3_CODE" = "COUNTRY_CODE")) %>%

  (co_comb_pass %>%

  (lat_proxy %>% select(COUNTRY, iso3, combined_cluster) %>%
     magrittr::set_colnames(c("COUNTRY","COUNTRY_CODE", "combined_cluster")) %>%
     mutate(cluster_type = "proxy"))
) %>% left_join(world.country.avg.lat.long %>% select(COUNTRY, mean_lat, mean_long), by = "COUNTRY") %>% 
  left_join(co %>% select(COUNTRY, ITZ)) %>% #itz)) #### CHECK: does "itz" need to be capitalized
  distinct()

# Combined cluster map who
combined_cluster_map_who <- who_shp %>%
  left_join(combined_cluster_map, by = c("ISO_3_CODE" = "COUNTRY_CODE")) %>%
  mutate(COUNTRY_CLEAN = gsub(x = CNTRY_TERR, pattern = "'", replacement = ""),
         centroid = st_centroid(geometry),
         centroid = st_coordinates(centroid),
         centroid_ml = centroid[,"Y"]) %>%
  mutate(
    cluster_type = if_else(
      is.na(cluster_type) & is.nan(centroid_ml) == F,
      "proxy",
      cluster_type
    )
  )

combined_cluster_map_who$centroid_cl <- sapply(combined_cluster_map_who$centroid_ml, function(x){
  if(is.na(x) | is.nan(x)) {
    return(x)
  } else {
    return(cluster.avg.lat.long$combined_cluster[which.min(abs(x - cluster.avg.lat.long$cl_mean_lat))])
  }
})

combined_cluster_map_who <- combined_cluster_map_who %>%
  mutate(combined_cluster = coalesce(combined_cluster, centroid_cl))
```

From these analyses **111** countries were used to establish the initial
draft clusters (the `*_pass` partitions used for consensus clustering
and the cluster/country-level burden-curve GAMs above). The initial
influenza testing data had **180** countries listed. From that broader
set, **150** countries had estimated country-period GAMs in Section 3
(used to compute `inf_all_burden`) -- a larger set than the 111
countries retained for clustering, since it also includes countries that
passed the basic detection/weeks-reported thresholds but lacked the \>=5
years of data required for the consensus ensemble. The final dataset
with latitudinal cluster proxying has all **253** countries with a
cluster assignment. These assignments may be refined in the future with
continuing years of data from countries and the possible inclusion of
more countries into the primary analysis.

We will then generate tables of information for cluster distributions
for outside use.


### 6.1 Assessment of Latitudinal Proxying by Leave One Out Analysis

After generating the tables of distributions, we completed a
leave-one-out analysis to assess the validity of assigning countries
with insufficient data to clusters by latitudinal proxying. The leave
one out was conducted by sequentially leaving countries out of each
analysis partition, recomputing the entire clustering using the same
algorithms and resampling as the final result runs, and then proxying
the country that was left out to closest cluster mean latitude. First,
we need to save the necessary data into an `.Rdata` bundle, in order to
offload the compute outside of the Rmarkdown document.

```{r}
# Save the necessary objects to file to complete a leave-one-out analysis
# assessing latitudinal proxying
# This packages up everything the LOO cluster script needs into ONE .RData
# file: the RAW data for both partitions, each partition's chosen final clustering
# labels, and a latitude lookup table.

# Raw data frames for each partition required:
# These should be your original raw data frames with columns:
#   COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, YEAR, WEEK, inf_all_burden (calendar)
#   COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, shifted_year, shifted_week, inf_all_burden (shifted)
raw_df_list <- list(
  co_cy_pass = co_cy_pass,
  co_sy_pass = co_sy_pass
)

# Original final clustering labels for each partition:
original_labels_list <- list(
  co_cy_pass = final_calendar_clustering$labels,
  co_sy_pass = final_shifted_clustering$labels
)

# Latitude lookup table:
lat_lookup <- world.country.avg.lat.long %>%
  mutate(country_code = iso3,
         latitude = mean_lat)

lat_lookup_list <- list(
  co_cy_pass = lat_lookup,
  co_sy_pass = lat_lookup
)

# Checks before saving
for (p in names(raw_df_list)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n--- Checking partition: %s ---\n", p))

  raw_df <- raw_df_list[[p]]
  labels <- original_labels_list[[p]]
  lat_lkp <- lat_lookup_list[[p]]

  # Check raw_df has the columns standardize_columns() will need
  has_cy_cols <- all(c("YEAR", "WEEK") %in% names(raw_df))
  has_sy_cols <- all(c("shifted_year", "shifted_week") %in% names(raw_df))
  cat(sprintf("  Has calendar columns (YEAR, WEEK): %s\n", has_cy_cols))
  cat(sprintf("  Has shifted columns (shifted_year, shifted_week): %s\n", has_sy_cols))
  cat(sprintf("  Has COUNTRY, COUNTRY_CODE, inf_all_burden: %s\n",
              all(c("COUNTRY", "COUNTRY_CODE", "inf_all_burden") %in% names(raw_df))))

  # Check labels is a named vector
  cat(sprintf("  original_labels: %d countries, named vector: %s\n",
              length(labels), !is.null(names(labels))))

  # Check lat_lookup has required columns
  cat(sprintf("  lat_lookup: %d rows, has country_code/latitude columns: %s\n",
              nrow(lat_lkp), all(c("country_code", "latitude") %in% names(lat_lkp))))

  # Check for countries in labels but missing from lat_lookup (these will
  # produce NA latitude-proxy results, worth knowing about upfront)
  missing_lat <- setdiff(names(labels), lat_lkp$country_code)
  if (length(missing_lat) > 0) {
    cat(sprintf("  WARNING: %d countries in original_labels have NO latitude entry: %s\n",
                length(missing_lat), paste(missing_lat, collapse = ", ")))
  }
}

# Save the bundle
save(raw_df_list, original_labels_list, lat_lookup_list,
     file = "data/loo_input_bundle.RData")

cat("\n=== Bundle saved to data/loo_input_bundle.RData ===\n")
cat(sprintf("File size: %.1f MB\n", file.size("data/loo_input_bundle.RData") / 1e6))
```

The scripts to conduct the compute is located in
[`scripts/loo_analysis.R`](scripts/loo_analysis.R) and
[`scripts/loo_analysis_alignment.R`](scripts/loo_analysis_alignment.R).
The first script conducts the leave one out analysis run itself and
saves all the run results. The second script
(`scripts/loo_analysis_alignment.R`) loads all the computed results and
aligns each analysis clustering run with the original analysis
clustering by consensus grouping, as clustering number assignment is
arbitrary. This way we can easily assess the percentage of countries
that are assigned to their original cluster via latitudinal proxying,
and also the run to run variation in clustering assignment for countries
included in each run.

The following are accessory functions to the leave one out analysis:

```{r}
# Load a consolidated LOO .RData file:
# Returns a named list matching the cluster script's saved structure:
#   loo_results: loo_results[[partition]][[country]], nested list
#   loo_summary: flat data frame, one row per (partition, country)
#   loo_run_metadata: loo_run_metadata[[partition]], settings used per partition
#   country_lookups: country_lookups[[partition]]
#   original_labels_list: original_labels_list[[partition]] (needed by
#    the alignment/stability functions below)
#   lat_lookups: lat_lookups[[partition]]
load_loo_results <- function(rdata_path) {
  if (!file.exists(rdata_path)) stop("LOO results file not found: ", rdata_path)

  e <- new.env()
  loaded_names <- load(rdata_path, envir = e)

  required <- c("loo_results", "loo_summary", "loo_run_metadata")
  missing <- setdiff(required, loaded_names)
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    stop("LOO results file is missing expected objects: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  }

  cat("Loaded LOO analysis results:\n")
  for (p in names(e$loo_run_metadata)) {
    if (p == "total_elapsed_hours") next
    meta <- e$loo_run_metadata[[p]]
    cat(sprintf("  [%s] dataset_type=%s | algo=%s | k=%d | final=%s | n_boot=%d | resample_pct=%.2f | n_countries=%d\n",
                p, meta$dataset_type %||% "NA", meta$chosen_algo, meta$k_final, meta$final_algorithm,
                meta$n_boot, meta$resample_pct, meta$n_countries))
  }
  if (!is.null(e$loo_run_metadata$total_elapsed_hours)) {
    cat(sprintf("  Total elapsed: %.2f hours\n", e$loo_run_metadata$total_elapsed_hours))
  }
  cat(sprintf("  Successful: %d / %d\n", sum(e$loo_summary$loo_rerun_succeeded), nrow(e$loo_summary)))

  as.list(e)
}

# Align LOO run labels to the ORIGINAL clustering:
# Each LOO run's cluster labels are arbitrary. Before any
# cross-run comparison is meaningful, every LOO run's labels must be mapped
# onto the original final clustering's numbering via best-overlap matching.
align_loo_labels_to_original <- function(loo_labels, original_labels) {
  common <- intersect(names(loo_labels), names(original_labels))
  if (length(common) == 0) return(NULL)

  overlap <- table(loo_labels[common], original_labels[common])

  mapping <- c()
  used_original <- c()
  for (r in rownames(overlap)[order(-apply(overlap, 1, max))]) {
    candidates <- overlap[r, ]
    candidates[names(candidates) %in% used_original] <- -1
    best_original <- names(candidates)[which.max(candidates)]
    mapping[r] <- best_original
    used_original <- c(used_original, best_original)
  }

  aligned <- as.integer(mapping[as.character(loo_labels)])
  names(aligned) <- names(loo_labels)
  aligned
}

# Verify label correspondence quality for every LOO run:
# For each LOO run, reports how well its aligned labels actually agree with
# the original clustering (via ARI, computed on the aligned labels vs.
# original, over the common countries). A low ARI here means the rest of the
# partition reorganized substantially when that country was excluded.
verify_loo_label_correspondence <- function(loo_data) {
  results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(loo_data$loo_results), function(partition_name) {
    partition_results <- loo_data$loo_results[[partition_name]]
    original_labels <- loo_data$original_labels_list[[partition_name]]

    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(partition_results), function(excluded) {
      entry <- partition_results[[excluded]]
      if (!entry$succeeded) {
        return(data.frame(partition = partition_name, excluded_country = excluded,
                           n_common = NA, ari = NA, note = "LOO run failed"))
      }

      aligned <- align_loo_labels_to_original(entry$final$labels, original_labels)
      common <- intersect(names(aligned), names(original_labels))
      ari <- compute_ari(aligned, original_labels)

      data.frame(partition = partition_name, excluded_country = excluded,
                 n_common = length(common), ari = round(ari, 4), note = NA)
    }))
  }))

  rownames(results) <- NULL
  cat("Label correspondence (aligned LOO labels vs. original clustering) by run:\n")
  print(results)
  cat(sprintf("\nMean ARI across all successful LOO runs: %.4f\n", mean(results$ari, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat("Runs with notably LOW ARI indicate the partition reorganized substantially\n")
  cat("when that country was excluded -- worth inspecting those specifically.\n")

  results
}

## Cross-LOO-run membership stability per country:
## For every country, across every LOO run where it was NOT the excluded one,
## records which (ALIGNED) cluster it landed in. Summarizes as: the country's
## MODAL (most common) aligned cluster across all those runs, and a stability
## score = the fraction of runs where it landed in that modal cluster (1.0 =
## perfectly consistent across every LOO run; lower = the country's cluster
## assignment is sensitive to which other country gets excluded).
##
## This is conceptually parallel to compute_raw_cluster_tally()'s shift_score,
## but the axis of perturbation here is "which country was excluded from the
## WHOLE ensemble rebuild," rather than "which bootstrap resample."
compute_loo_membership_stability <- function(loo_data, partition_name) {
  partition_results <- loo_data$loo_results[[partition_name]]
  original_labels <- loo_data$original_labels_list[[partition_name]]
  all_countries <- names(original_labels)

  # tally[country, cluster] = number of LOO runs (excluding ones where this
  # country itself was the excluded one, since it has no assignment then)
  # where this country landed in that ALIGNED cluster
  k <- length(unique(original_labels))
  tally <- matrix(0, nrow = length(all_countries), ncol = k,
                   dimnames = list(all_countries, paste0("cluster_", seq_len(k))))
  n_runs_present <- setNames(rep(0, length(all_countries)), all_countries)

  for (excluded in names(partition_results)) {
    entry <- partition_results[[excluded]]
    if (!entry$succeeded) next

    aligned <- align_loo_labels_to_original(entry$final$labels, original_labels)
    if (is.null(aligned)) next

    for (c in names(aligned)) {
      cl <- aligned[c]
      if (is.na(cl) || cl < 1 || cl > k) next
      tally[c, cl] <- tally[c, cl] + 1
      n_runs_present[c] <- n_runs_present[c] + 1
    }
  }

  tally_df <- as.data.frame(tally)
  tally_df$country_code <- rownames(tally_df)
  tally_df$n_loo_runs_present <- n_runs_present[rownames(tally_df)]
  tally_df$original_cluster <- original_labels[rownames(tally_df)]

  tally_df$modal_cluster <- apply(tally[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE], 1, function(x) {
    if (sum(x) == 0) return(NA)
    which.max(x)
  })
  tally_df$stability_score <- apply(tally[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE], 1, function(x) {
    if (sum(x) == 0) return(NA)
    max(x) / sum(x)
  })
  tally_df$modal_matches_original <- tally_df$modal_cluster == tally_df$original_cluster

  tally_df <- tally_df %>%
    select(country_code, original_cluster, modal_cluster, modal_matches_original,
           stability_score, n_loo_runs_present, everything()) %>%
    arrange(stability_score)

  cat(sprintf("\nLOO membership stability for partition '%s' (k = %d):\n", partition_name, k))
  cat(sprintf("Mean stability score across all countries: %.3f\n", mean(tally_df$stability_score, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("Countries whose modal LOO cluster does NOT match their original cluster: %d / %d\n",
              sum(!tally_df$modal_matches_original, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(tally_df)))
  cat("\nLeast stable countries (lowest stability_score):\n")
  print(head(tally_df[, c("country_code", "original_cluster", "modal_cluster", "modal_matches_original", "stability_score", "n_loo_runs_present")], 10))

  tally_df
}
```

After completing the analysis run and alignment we can then load the
results (`data/loo_analysis_final_corrected.RData`) for assessment.

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
loo_data <- load_loo_results("data/loo_analysis_final_corrected.RData")

# Overall mean rate of proxying success
loo_mean <- loo_data$loo_summary %>%
  summarise(m = sum(original_cluster == proxy_cluster)/length(original_cluster))

# --- Quick look at the overall summary across both partitions ---
loo_data$loo_summary %>%
  mutate(combinded_cluster = case_when(partition == "co_sy_pass" & original_cluster == 1 ~ "A",
                                       partition == "co_sy_pass" & original_cluster == 2 ~ "C",
                                       partition == "co_sy_pass" & original_cluster == 3 ~ "B",
                                       partition == "co_cy_pass" & original_cluster == 1 ~ "E",
                                       partition == "co_cy_pass" & original_cluster == 2 ~ "D")) %>%
  group_by(combinded_cluster, partition, original_cluster) %>%
  summarise(n_countries = n(),
            n_lat_proxy_match = sum(original_cluster == proxy_cluster),
            perc_proxy_match = n_lat_proxy_match/n_countries) %>%
  kable(format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

From the results of the leave one out analysis we can see a high level
of congruence between the final "original cluster" and the leave one out
run "modal" cluster with an overall proxying match rate of
`r round(loo_mean$m, 3)*100`%. With a minimum of 68.4% (combined cluster
D) and maximum of 86.4% (combined cluster C) of intracluster proxying
match rates.

We can also evaluate the stability of the clusters from run to run in
the leave one out analysis.

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
correspondence <- verify_loo_label_correspondence(loo_data)

stability_cy <- compute_loo_membership_stability(loo_data, partition_name = "co_cy_pass")

stability_cy %>%
  mutate(combined_cluster = case_when(original_cluster == 1 ~ "E",
                                      original_cluster == 2 ~ "D")) %>%
  relocate(combined_cluster) %>%
  kable(format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
stability_sy <- compute_loo_membership_stability(loo_data, partition_name = "co_sy_pass")

stability_sy %>%
  mutate(combined_cluster = case_when(original_cluster == 1 ~ "A",
                                      original_cluster == 2 ~ "C",
                                      original_cluster == 3 ~ "B")) %>%
  relocate(combined_cluster) %>%
  kable(format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  scroll_box(height = "400px")
```

From the totality of the leave one out analysis only one country,
Georgia (GEO), switched to a different cluster, from combined cluster B
to combined cluster A. This was not unexpected, as the final consensus
result for this country was borderline between these clusters. Out of
the 111 countries assessed in the leave one out analysis only 4 had
stability scores of less than 90%, with an overall mean stability score
of 98.9%. This gives us confidence that the chosen method is robust in
it's assignment.

Regional and sub-regional groupings used in the country-level summaries
below follow the UN Statistics Division's M49 standard country
classification [@unsd_m49].

```{r}


##Descriptive analyses of country clusters

#If starting anew, pull in saved final tsv file
#combined_cluster_map <- read_tsv("data/co_cluster_mapping.tsv")

#Import UN geoschemes to use as regional unit of analysis
un <- read_csv("data/UNSD_geoschemes.csv") %>%
  rename(REGION = `Region Name`,
         SUBREGION = `Sub-region Name`,
         INTREGION = `Intermediate Region Name`,
         COUNTRY = `Country or Area`,
         COUNTRY_CODE = `ISO-alpha3 Code`) %>%
  select(REGION, SUBREGION, INTREGION, COUNTRY_CODE, COUNTRY) %>%
  mutate(INTREGION = ifelse(is.na(INTREGION), SUBREGION, INTREGION))

# Align UN and cluster map datasets to maximize geographic coverage
combined_cluster_map_data_1 <- combined_cluster_map %>%
  mutate(COUNTRY_CODE = case_when(COUNTRY == "Chagos Archipelago" ~ "IOT", 
                                  COUNTRY %in% c("Saba", "Sint Eustatius", "Bonaire") ~ "BES",
                                  COUNTRY == "Heard Island" ~ "HMD",
                                  TRUE ~ COUNTRY_CODE)) %>%
  filter(!COUNTRY %in% c("Bonaire", "Saba")) %>%
  mutate(COUNTRY = case_when(COUNTRY_CODE == "BES" ~ "Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba",
                             COUNTRY_CODE == "HMD" ~ "Heard Island and McDonald Islands",
                             TRUE ~ COUNTRY))

clusters <- un %>%
  full_join(combined_cluster_map_data_1, by = "COUNTRY_CODE") %>%
  select(-c(COUNTRY.x, SUBREGION)) %>%
  rename(COUNTRY = COUNTRY.y) %>%
  mutate(REGION = case_when(COUNTRY == "Kosovo" ~ "Europe",
                            COUNTRY =="Taiwan" ~ "Asia",
                            TRUE ~ REGION),
         INTREGION = case_when(COUNTRY %in% c("Kosovo") ~ "Southern Europe",
                               COUNTRY %in% c("Azores", "Madeira Islands", "Canary Islands") ~ "Macaronesia",
                               COUNTRY == "Taiwan" ~ "Eastern Asia",
                               TRUE ~ INTREGION),
         COUNTRY = case_when(COUNTRY_CODE == "MAC" ~ "China, Macao Special Administrative Region",
                             COUNTRY_CODE == "ALA" ~ "Åland Islands",
                             COUNTRY_CODE == "SJM" ~ "Svalbard and Jan Mayen Islands",
                             COUNTRY_CODE == "GIB" ~ "Gibraltar",
                             COUNTRY_CODE == "TKL" ~ "Tokelau",
                             COUNTRY_CODE == "TUV" ~ "Tuvalu",
                             COUNTRY_CODE == "UMI" ~ "United States Minor Outlying Islands",
                             TRUE ~ COUNTRY),
         combined_cluster = case_when(COUNTRY_CODE == "MAC" ~ "B", #felt comfortable manually coding these territories since they are
                                     COUNTRY_CODE %in% c("ALA", "SJM", "GIB") ~ "A", # within countries with original assigned zones
                                     TRUE ~ combined_cluster),
         cluster_type = ifelse(COUNTRY_CODE %in% c("MAC", "ALA", "SJM", "GIB", "UMI", "TUV", "TKL"), "proxy", cluster_type)) %>% 
  filter(!COUNTRY %in% c("Siachen Glacier", "Ascension Island", "Barbuda", "Grenadines")) %>%
  filter(!COUNTRY_CODE %in% c("BVT"))
```

```{r}
### Supplemental table: 
### - Country
### - Population-weighted mean latitude
### - Epidemic zone assignment
### - Epidemic zone was based on original analysis or proxy
### - Calendar weeks in which most influenza detections occurred
orig_co_activityrange <- epidemic_thresholds_co %>% ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(orig_range = paste0(month.name[epidemic_start_month], "-", month.name[epidemic_end_month])) %>% 
  select(COUNTRY, orig_range)

proxy_co_activityrange <- epidemic_thresholds %>% ungroup() %>%  
  mutate(proxy_range = paste0(month.name[epidemic_start_month], "-", month.name[epidemic_end_month])) %>% 
  select(combined_cluster, proxy_range)


supp_tbl2_clusterlatrange <- clusters %>%
  select(COUNTRY, mean_lat, cluster_type, combined_cluster) %>% 
  left_join(., orig_co_activityrange, by = "COUNTRY") %>% 
  left_join(., proxy_co_activityrange, by = "combined_cluster") %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(month_range = case_when(cluster_type == "original" ~ orig_range, 
                                 cluster_type == "proxy" ~ paste0("[",proxy_range, "]")))  %>% 
  arrange(combined_cluster, -mean_lat) %>% 
  left_join(tbl_exclusions2, by = "COUNTRY")

write.csv(supp_tbl2_clusterlatrange, "data/supp_table2_co_latcluster.csv")
```

Table of sub-regions in each cluster. This helps us populate the
Results section of the manuscript. There are 2 tables made: one for
original analysis and one for the proxy countries.

*Original countries:*

```{r}
### Dealing with original analysis countries first

original_regions <- clusters %>% filter(cluster_type == "original") %>% 
  select(combined_cluster, COUNTRY, INTREGION, mean_lat) %>% distinct() %>% 
  mutate(INTREGION = factor(INTREGION))

original_regions$INTREGION <- fct_reorder(original_regions$INTREGION, -original_regions$mean_lat)

original_regions %>% 
  select(-COUNTRY, -mean_lat) %>% 
  tbl_summary(by = combined_cluster, 
              statistic = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)")
```

*Proxy countries:*

```{r}
### Dealing with countries assigned to cluster by proxy

proxy_regions <- clusters %>% filter(cluster_type == "proxy") %>% 
  select(combined_cluster, COUNTRY, INTREGION, mean_lat) %>% distinct() %>% 
  mutate(INTREGION = factor(INTREGION))

proxy_regions$INTREGION <- fct_reorder(proxy_regions$INTREGION, -proxy_regions$mean_lat)

proxy_regions %>% 
  select(-COUNTRY, -mean_lat) %>% 
  tbl_summary(by = combined_cluster, 
              statistic = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)")


```

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%"}
  draw_label(
    "Shifted Year Partition Assessment",
    fontface = 'bold',
    size = 16,
    x = 0.5,      # Centers the title horizontally
    hjust = 0.5   # Centers the text anchor
  )

s2b_plot_final <- plot_grid(s2b_title, s2b_plot, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))

s2_plot_final <- plot_grid(s2a_plot_final, s2b_plot_final, ncol = 1)

ggsave("plots/s_figure_2.pdf", s2_plot_final, units = "in", height = 11, width = 8.5)
```

```{r out.width="100%", out.height="100%", cache=TRUE}
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("A" = "#DF5C24",
```
